rule: A section scaffold is not atomic coverage. Only listed requirements have been extracted; all other clauses remain unaudited. Partial means observed behavior on the recorded target, not cross-platform conformance.

requirements.statement: Each renderer declares capabilities and validator profile; unsupported capabilities produce a diagnostic or documented data-preserving fallback.
requirements.next: A conservative family/target declaration names the Kotlin validator and three browser-only fallbacks; focused JVM fallback suites pass. Add per-renderer option and target evidence, registration ranks and broader unsupported diagnostics.

requirements.statement: The serialized UI-model shape and behavior are the portable contract; Kotlin types may differ from TypeScript reference declarations.
requirements.next: A mixed authored document round-trips known layout/control/presentation elements, named TemplateLayout/Slot payloads, rules and flat options through the demo editor on JVM and iOS simulator. Verify broader wire vectors and browser/Android runtime behavior.

requirements.statement: The extension should avoid changes to JSON Forms core; a wrapper or resolution layer may preprocess extended elements before tester dispatch.
requirements.next: Audit current core changes and record any justified deviation.

requirements.statement: Portable model semantics must be reproduced by each declared Kotlin renderer family.
requirements.next: Map every portable option to Material/Cupertino behavior and target evidence.

requirements.statement: Common JSON Forms behaviors and renderer enhancements should be supported where applicable, with deviations documented.
requirements.next: Record applicability and evidence for multi/date formats and schema-aware date limits.

requirements.statement: Renderer and runtime escape hatches are preserved as authored data; execution or interpretation is limited to a matching, permitted contract.
requirements.next: The demo editor preserves a Button script and React/Svelte/vendor options through parse, apply and re-emit on JVM. Mounted Material/Cupertino Button tests on JVM and iOS simulator ignore nonmatching renderer namespaces and require explicit permission before executing a parsed script. Audit other escape hatches and verify browser, Wasm and Android behavior.

requirements.statement: Unknown renderer namespaces are preserved and ignored by non-matching renderer families.
requirements.next: A VendorWidget with name, vendor options, payload and explicitly empty elements/options survives parser/editor round trip; mounted Material/Cupertino JVM hosts show the unsupported fallback without writes. Parsed Buttons ignore nonmatching React/Svelte option namespaces on JVM and iOS simulator. Verify imported unknown namespaces, browser/Wasm/Android UI and richer nested children.

requirements.statement: Global core conventions stay top-level, portable extension config uses jsonformsExtended, and implementation-only config uses a declared vendor namespace.
requirements.next: Audit every config reader and add precedence tests.

requirements.statement: Per-element options remain flat; only global config is namespaced, including options used by renderer testers.
requirements.next: Serialized flat toggle selects the Material/Cupertino switch tester; the same value inside options.jsonformsExtended is retained but does not select it. Mounted JVM/iOS cases switch from checkbox to switch only on flat-option change without a data write. Audit other selection-bearing options and browser/Android targets.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Established names that stay at the top level
requirements.statement: Established global names showUnfocusedDescription, hideRequiredAsterisk, disableAdd, disableRemove and restrict remain top-level.
requirements.next: Array action flags use top-level config with explicit local false precedence. Core no longer injects restrict:false when the host omits it. Mounted Material/Cupertino JVM cases distinguish top-level showUnfocusedDescription and hideRequiredAsterisk from opposite namespaced values during a live config change. Audit all remaining readers and verify non-JVM mounted behavior.

requirements.statement: Global layoutDefaults, dynamicValues, dynamic, security, markup and confirmation live under jsonformsExtended.
requirements.next: Serialized layoutDefaults and confirmation plus dynamicValues, mounted security and markup reject misplaced aliases on JVM. Audit the dynamic block and remaining consumers and verify target platforms.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Namespace keys are literals on the wire.
requirements.statement: Namespace keys are literal wire names and implementations read only their declared locations.
requirements.next: Literal jsonformsExtended and wrong-case/top-level placement are covered for five blocks on JVM; audit dynamic and other namespace readers, then verify browser and native targets.

requirements.statement: name is a top-level portable element field used as stable model identity, never options.name or a renderer label.
requirements.next: Test all standard element types and reference resolution.

requirements.statement: Element names must not be translated or derived from translated labels.
requirements.next: Mounted Material/Cupertino JVM and iOS simulator cases preserve a named Category selection while its English/Bulgarian label changes, allow selection through translated labels, and make no form write. Mounted Template/Slot cases on those targets keep both reference names stable while the supplied heading changes language. Verify other named elements and JS, Wasm and Android behavior.

requirements.statement: Name uniqueness is scoped to the referencing construct; duplicates within that construct must be diagnosed without positional resolution.
requirements.next: Duplicate Template registry names now report and render no positional winner; duplicate supplied Slot names report and render the slot fallback; duplicate Category names report and cannot resolve an initial name by position. Separate Categorizations may each use the same name without diagnostics. Material/Cupertino mounted JVM and iOS simulator tests pass; the full core JS and Wasm browser suites pass with the pure Category resolver test. Dynamic Template registry replacement also updates ambiguous/unique rendering on JVM and iOS without a form write. Verify mounted JS/Wasm and Android behavior.

requirements.statement: A portable action adapter normalizes missing optional parameters to an empty object.
requirements.next: Paired mounted Material/Cupertino JVM tests parse an action Button with omitted params and receive an empty JSON object through both the event and legacy handler, without a form write. Verify other targets and host action adapters.

requirements.statement: The DOM Element and $el members of the web ActionEvent are web-specific and need no Kotlin rendering implementation.
requirements.next: Keep the exclusion explicit in capability declarations.

requirements.statement: The portable action event exposes the host's external context alongside a live form-state snapshot.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM tests pass and replace arbitrary host context, including external and additional errors, without mutating earlier event snapshots. The webcomponent accepts a JSON context attribute and forwards it with live state and validation fields; its registration tests and Kotlin/JS compilation pass. The browser executable link twice exhausted disk before mounted interaction, and non-JVM action interaction remains to verify.

requirements.statement: New UI element types are a last resort; use the existing representation for each listed concept.
requirements.next: The model/serializer audit maps listed concepts to established types and keeps spec Button in unknown-element passthrough; complete option/target conformance and audit all future custom types.

requirements.statement: Editable/viewable data uses Control.
requirements.next: Serialized Control mapping and mounted Material/Cupertino editing pass on JVM, JS and Wasm; verify iOS and Android runtime plus broader view-only formats.

requirements.statement: Horizontal and vertical structure uses existing layout elements.
requirements.next: Serialized horizontal and vertical layout nesting and mounted Material/Cupertino controls pass on JVM, JS and Wasm; verify iOS and Android runtime.

requirements.statement: A bounded section uses Group.
requirements.next: Serialized Group nesting and mounted Material/Cupertino rendering pass on JVM, JS and Wasm; verify iOS and Android runtime and bounded-section presentation.

requirements.statement: A collapsible section uses Group with collapsible.
requirements.next: A serialized Group fixture with options.collapsible=true parses to GroupElement and closes/reopens its field without writing data in both renderer families. All 14 cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser; the full mounted browser suites pass 2,082 JS and 2,085 Wasm tests with zero failures/skips. Verify Android runtime before calling the portable requirement complete.

requirements.statement: Tabs, steppers and accordions use Categorization, with variant for stepper and accordion.
requirements.next: The pinned fixture maps default tabs, stepper and accordion to three CategorizationElements. Paired mounted tests navigate Planning/Contact, toggle the authored initially open accordion, preserve data and verify English/Bulgarian status and rule changes. Both cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser. Verify Android runtime before calling the portable requirement complete.

requirements.statement: Chips, multi-select, table, switch, slider and code-editor presentations use Control plus options.
requirements.next: A serialized six-Control matrix preserves chips/multi-select variant strings, table/toggle/slider JSON booleans and code format/language strings. The parser class passes on JVM/iOS and full core JS/Wasm browser suites. Mounted examples and extended-renderer browser suites pass. Both Web Component bundles show editor.monacoUnavailable and native editing fallback in Chrome without a data write; this is not a Monaco engine. Audit the complete six-presentation mounted matrix on Android and require a disposable DOM adapter before claiming browser-only code-engine conformance.

requirements.statement: Interpolated rich text uses an internationalizable element with text options.
requirements.next: The pinned fixture maps interpolated and Markdown labels to internationalizable LabelElements with textParams, interpolate and markup options intact. Paired Material/Cupertino mounted fixture tests pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser, including data and English/Bulgarian locale changes with no diagnostics. Verify Android runtime before calling the portable requirement complete.

requirements.statement: Images use ImageView.
requirements.next: The pinned fixture maps static, scoped and decorative images to ImageViewElements. Paired Material/Cupertino mounted tests confirm image accessibility, rule/data updates and no writes on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser. Verify Android runtime before closing the portable mapping.

requirements.statement: Visual dividers use Separator.
requirements.next: The pinned fixture maps two visual dividers to SeparatorElements; paired Material/Cupertino mounted tests keep both horizontal divider semantics through image data changes with no writes on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser. Separate mounted tests cover vertical geometry and visibility. Verify Android runtime before closing the portable mapping.

requirements.statement: Whitespace and flexible push use Spacer.
requirements.next: The pinned fixture maps absent, 64 and zero size values to SpacerElements. Paired Material/Cupertino mounted tests measure 32 pixel default and 64 pixel authored spacing relative to zero without writes on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser. Existing mounted geometry tests cover flexible weighted push. Verify Android runtime before closing the portable mapping.

requirements.statement: Commands use Button.
requirements.next: The pinned fixture maps English/Bulgarian Button elements with authored setLocale actions and params. Paired Material/Cupertino mounted tests emit both host events with en/bg params and no data writes on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser. Verify Android runtime before closing the portable mapping.

requirements.statement: Navigation uses Link.
requirements.next: The pinned fixture maps allowed, empty and policy-refused destinations to LinkElements. Paired Material/Cupertino mounted tests open the allowed URI, keep empty/refused destinations inert, report the refusal and make no data write on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser. Verify Android runtime before closing the portable mapping.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Deferred, and deliberately not specified here
requirements.statement: Progress indicators, explicit breakpoint overrides, grid start, validation-gated wizard semantics and richer divider features are deferred outside the portable contract.
requirements.next: Do not treat these deferred concepts as portable conformance gaps without a later specification amendment.

requirements.statement: Retain established JSON Forms presentation encodings; one canonical encoding per presentation, without equivalent aliases.
requirements.next: Autocomplete uses one strict boolean option and defaults off in enum/oneOf renderers. The shared option tester preserves JSON scalar types: quoted true/numeric strings cannot select Boolean/numeric options, and one Number branch handles JVM/Native/JS decimals consistently. Paired mounted Boolean fixture tests show options.switch and quoted toggle use checkbox, while authored toggle:true uses switch on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm. Full core suites pass 577 JVM and 576 each JS/Wasm browser tests (13 existing skips per target); mounted browser suites pass 2,082 JS and 2,085 Wasm with zero skips/failures. Audit other aliases/precedence and Android runtime.

requirements.statement: Multiline text selects via options.multi: true on string.
requirements.next: Both renderer families select multi:true and mounted JVM/iOS fixture cases retain multiline text. Compact plain-string table cells now select multiline for multi:true; four paired mounted cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser, including newline storage, invalid imports, restriction, host replacement and live Bulgarian feedback. Specialized string contracts stay on the existing renderer path. Verify physical IME newline behavior, layout geometry and device accessibility.

requirements.statement: Masked string selects via options.mask on string.
requirements.next: Ten mounted Material/Cupertino fixture cases pass on JVM and iOS simulator, including character-by-character booking and prefixed phone entry, Backspace, and mid-string insertion/removal at a selected display offset. Shared visual transformation maps raw caret offsets; pure JVM tests cover separators, phone prefix and invalid import identity. Verify arrow navigation across literals, accessibility and browser/device interaction.

requirements.statement: Boolean switch selects via options.toggle: true on boolean.
requirements.next: Authored fixture cases pass in Material/Cupertino on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser: toggle:true selects a switch, ordinary boolean selects a checkbox, false/true/missing/numeric-zero identity survives, and checkbox groups preserve membership/orientation. A paired mounted case confirms options.switch and quoted toggle remain checkboxes while canonical JSON Boolean selects a switch on all four targets. Base cell registries dispatch compact native checkbox/switch cells. Verify Android runtime and physical keyboard, pointer and screen-reader interaction.

requirements.statement: Radio choices selects via options.format: "radio" on supported enum/oneOf choices.
requirements.next: The authored fixture passes on JVM, iOS simulator and JS browser in Material and Cupertino: enum and oneOf radio selection, row/stack layout, numeric and constant storage, missing and imported unknown choices, structural object/array equality, and Arrow/Space keyboard selection. Verify pointer and screen-reader interaction on devices/browsers.

requirements.statement: Searchable choices selects via options.autocomplete: true on supported finite choices.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM/iOS and imported JS browser Material/Cupertino enum and oneOf cases verify opt-in search, nonsearchable default and label-to-constant selection; JVM/iOS cases also cover pending drafts, imported unknown preservation and host replacement. Verify keyboard, pointer and screen-reader interaction on devices/browsers.

requirements.statement: Slider selects via options.slider: true on range-qualified number/integer.
requirements.next: The authored range-qualified number selects Material/Cupertino sliders on JVM, iOS simulator and JS browser, while the ordinary integer control does not. The range tester now requires JSON Boolean slider true and rejects the quoted string. Mounted compact table cells pass JVM, iOS, JS and Wasm cases for imported invalid data, local status, host replacement and exact integer steps. Verify keyboard, pointer and screen-reader interaction on devices/browsers.

requirements.statement: Colour selects via options.format: "color" or schema format: "color" on string.
requirements.next: Authored schema-format and UI-only options.format selection, Material/Cupertino RGB/HSB/default hex/hex3 preset storage, HSL/alpha import preservation, picker-only mode and invalid-import retention pass mounted JVM/iOS/JS browser tests. Verify Wasm/Android device interaction and the remaining §18.27 picker channel behavior.

requirements.statement: Password selects via options.format: "password" or schema format: "password" on string.
requirements.next: The authored schema-format and UI-only password controls pass Material/Cupertino mounted JVM, iOS simulator and JS browser tests. The same fixture verifies bounded OTP, unbounded OTP fallback, and table token edits without mount writes. Verify physical masking/accessibility, Android/Wasm interaction and full category navigation.

requirements.statement: Date selects via options.format: "date" or schema format: "date" on string.
requirements.next: The imported schema-selected date and UI-selected month controls pass Material/Cupertino JVM, iOS, JS browser and Wasm browser UI tests, including a YYYY.MM edit saved as YYYY-MM. Referenced object dates, authored tuple positions and a mixed string/null date also pass. A separate 2020-12 prefixItems date tuple proves date editor selection and positional storage on all four targets. Verify more picker bounds and device accessibility.

requirements.statement: Time selects via options.format: "time" or schema format: "time" on string.
requirements.next: Imported schema-selected time mounts without a write, UI-selected time saves HH:mm, schema-based seconds edit in the picker, and authored coarse time preserves its stored seconds in Material/Cupertino JVM, iOS, JS browser and Wasm browser UI tests. A seconds-bearing display format opens a seconds column without views. Verify remaining range constraints and device accessibility.

requirements.statement: Date and time selects via options.format: "date-time" or schema format: "date-time" on string.
requirements.next: Imported schema-selected date-time mounts without a write and UI-selected date-time retains its authored save format in Material/Cupertino JVM, iOS, JS browser and Wasm browser UI tests. The seconds-bearing date-time picker exposes a seconds column without views and saves its edit. Verify remaining range constraints and device accessibility.

requirements.statement: A new variant adds documented capability beyond renaming an established option.
requirements.next: Audited the added capability for stepper, accordion, chips, multi-select, OTP, tuple and splitter; AG Grid remains unsupported fallback. Verify all option consumers and target interactions before declaring every variant conformant.

requirements.statement: Password, date, time and date-time select from schema format even with generated UI schema.
requirements.next: Password generated-UI editing and all three temporal picker selections pass in both JVM families; test temporal storage/validation and non-JVM interactions.

requirements.statement: Password, date, time and date-time also select from UI options.format on a plain string schema.
requirements.next: Password UI-driven editing/storage and all three temporal picker selections pass in both JVM families; test temporal storage/validation and non-JVM interactions.

requirements.statement: UI presentation options do not rewrite the schema or disable its validation.
requirements.next: Paired Material/Cupertino mounted full-registry tests use UI format color over a string schema with minLength 7. A valid short color remains schema-invalid until the picker commits a long-enough color, then combined validity becomes Valid; the authored schema and sibling value stay unchanged. The focused JVM class passes and iOS simulator test sources compile. Extend to other presentation options and browser/native runtime.

requirements.statement: Custom save format remains compatible when schema declares a format.
requirements.next: Material/Cupertino date, time and date-time controls reject authored save patterns whose sample cannot satisfy the schema-declared format, report temporal.saveFormatIncompatible and use the schema-compatible default. Pure and six mounted cases pass on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm for incompatible date/month, time/minute and unzoned date-time patterns, valid storage and no mount writes. UI-only coarse save formats remain authored. Fourteen older temporal-cell/import cases pass on all four targets; the full examples-compose iOS suite passes after updating eight storage expectations. Verify other format-bearing controls and device interaction.

requirements.statement: Each schema/UI format conflict documents tester ranks and fallback.
requirements.next: The behavior catalog records Material/Cupertino tester ranks and first-entry tie precedence for date, time, date-time, password, color, duration, cron, file, code fallback and ordinary text. Two table-driven combined-registry and two mounted cases pass on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm with representative conflicts, fallbacks and retained time-schema validation after a date UI edit. Other format combinations and physical-device interaction remain open.

requirements.statement: Renderer and option provenance is declared; unverified fork support is labelled unverified, not upstream.
requirements.next: Add provenance to capability matrix and audit claims.

requirements.statement: Variant selects one presentation mode; independent behavior uses separate booleans, without duplicate encodings.
requirements.next: Portable variant remains distinct from Material input chrome and splitter requires an exact string; continue auditing independent flags and duplicate encodings across all renderer families.

requirements.statement: Local options override global defaults, preserving explicit false, zero and empty string.
requirements.next: A pure core test verifies local false, zero and empty-string values survive applied-map, layout, validation-indicator and dialog resolution on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm. Paired mounted Material/Cupertino help tests on those targets keep local false over global true without a write. Audit other option types.

requirements.sourceAnchor: **Renderer selection has a separate input contract.**
requirements.statement: Testers read UI-schema options; config stays separate and does not implicitly select multiline or other presentations.
requirements.next: Combined Material/Cupertino registry tests on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm show config-only format, multi and variant values do not select string presentations; an authored UI password format still wins over a conflicting config date value. Extend selection checks to array variants and other formats.

requirements.statement: Each structured option documents its own merge policy.
requirements.next: Documented the audited structured-option policies and typed Boolean behavior through table, choice and summary paths; focused JVM and full JS/Wasm core suites pass. Continue the remaining resolver inventory, mounted target checks and Android runtime.

requirements.statement: Merging preserves source config and authored UI-schema objects without mutation.
requirements.next: A pure core test passes on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm and preserves authored Control options, its nested dialog object, host config and nested layout/dialog defaults by identity and content after applied-map, layout, validation-indicator and dialog resolution. Audit other structured resolver paths and mounted host replacement.

requirements.statement: Dedicated read-only, confirmation and validator contracts supersede generic option precedence.
requirements.next: Cell readonly now uses the dedicated resolver so form/UI sources beat own false; the focused CellTest passes JVM/iOS and full core JS/Wasm suites. Confirmation tests preserve element/renderer/default precedence and core initialization uses an explicit validator option. Verify all renderer mutation paths before closing.

requirements.statement: Selection inspects the resolved schema at the control scope, including references and composition context.
requirements.next: Combined Material/Cupertino registry and mounted cases resolve distinct scoped array and scalar properties through allOf, anyOf, oneOf, then and else branches. Bounded data-aware dispatch chooses oneOf/anyOf editing branches from a unique stored JSON type or a uniquely matching required sibling const in the edited field's parent object, including nested property scopes and missing edited values. Numeric const comparisons use exact decimal value equality, including nested numeric values inside required object consts; equivalent spellings cannot identify separate branches. A branch-only field requires a unique sibling-const match; a stored type alone does not activate it. Shared or distinct flat alternative item fields form automatic table columns when a unique required scalar const identifies every branch and Add offers a branch choice. Authored columnDefs can name the union more broadly with per-row applicability. Imported rows with a missing or unknown discriminator can choose a branch without losing stored fields; focused composed-scope classes pass on JVM, iOS, JS browser and Wasm browser. Original whole-form validation remains authoritative. Verify other predicates, ambiguous matches, full browser suites and device interaction.

requirements.statement: Specialized renderer matches outrank generic fallbacks regardless of registration order.
requirements.next: Combined form-registry tests in both orders cover suggested string, finite oneOf/enum, password and bounded slider plus incompatible fallbacks. Combined cell-registry tests in both orders cover nine compact specialties, extended null/file feedback ownership and unclaimed incompatible cells. A mounted date-schema/password-cell conflict dispatches the ordinary date Control at the row path, retains an invalid draft without writing and commits a valid date once. Typed allOf/anyOf/oneOf properties keep their winners. Audit remaining specialties and mounted fallback combinations.

requirements.statement: Default array table presents primitives as one editable value per row, flat objects as columns, and nested objects as expandable details.
requirements.next: Material/Cupertino registry and mounted tests cover primitive cell editing, flat property columns, nested detail, and explicit table override. Shared flat fields across oneOf/anyOf item branches select an automatic table or explicit table; mounted cells select schemas per row and follow host replacement without an implicit write on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm. Flat branches with shared or distinct columns and a unique required scalar const discriminator select an automatic table with per-row editors and an Add branch menu that commits the chosen discriminator and authored defaults; numeric const uniqueness uses exact decimal equality. Imported rows with a missing or unknown discriminator retain their fields through branch repair; the focused composed-scope class passes on JVM, iOS, JS browser and Wasm browser. Ambiguous or nested alternatives retain expandable details; authored array-valued columnDefs can name their union more broadly. Config-only columnDefs leave the default layout. Earlier paired cases cover add/delete defaults, minItems validity and minLength repair across default shapes. Verify richer constraints, full browser suites, other predicates and device interaction.

requirements.statement: Explicit supported array variants override automatic fallback; item enum affects choice cells, not outer array renderer.
requirements.next: Combined-registry tests cover automatic checkbox, explicit table/grid fallback, chips/multi-select, tuple, referenced array/item schemas, referenced object-array ListWithDetail and config-only presentation values; mounted Material/Cupertino tables render enum choice cells. Verify the remaining composition contexts and actual browser AG Grid profile when a DOM-host lifecycle exists.

requirements.statement: Canonical additional variants are chips, multi-select, stepper and accordion; renderer additions must not rename canonical variants.
requirements.next: Full Material/Cupertino extended-registry tests select chips, multi-select, stepper and accordion by canonical names. Chips selects on free string arrays; multi-select falls back on non-finite arrays, chips falls back on integer arrays, and unsupported Categorization variants fall back to family tabs. Mounted tests cover all four presentations separately. Six paired mounted JVM fallback cases verify inapplicable multi-select and chips use ordinary array Add, retain existing values and write once; an unrelated Categorization variant uses tabs and switches panels without writing. The focused JVM class passes and iOS simulator test sources compile. Verify browser/native runtime before marking supported.

requirements.statement: Static authoring keeps canonical variants static; dynamic variant input belongs to the experimental overlay profile.
requirements.next: The pinned extended authoring schema accepts literal chips, multi-select, stepper and accordion variants and rejects $dynamic objects in Control and Categorization options.variant. The full authoring gate passes 194 local documents/registries. Complete Material/Cupertino registry tests select canonical array variants from literal Control options, not top-level config; a $dynamic-shaped object retains automatic checkbox selection. Focused JVM tests pass and iOS simulator test sources compile. The experimental overlay evaluator is outside the static profile; audit other dynamic-looking options and browser/native runtime before marking supported.

requirements.statement: Explicit chips and multi-select outrank automatic checkbox-group selection.
requirements.next: Explicit multi-select and chips rank above automatic checkboxes in both families; non-JVM interaction remains open.

requirements.sourceAnchor: What separates chips from a multi-select
requirements.statement: Chips use finite-item chooser or free-string entry based on item schema; multi-select requires uniqueItems, chips may preserve duplicates.
requirements.next: Pure and mounted JVM tests cover multi-select uniqueness and chips finite/free entry with duplicate tokens. Non-JVM interaction remains open.

requirements.statement: Removing a duplicate chip removes the acted-on occurrence by position.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM tests remove one acted-on duplicate through distinct positional accessibility names; verify other targets.

requirements.statement: Failed token lookup returns the array unchanged and cannot be reinterpreted as an index.
requirements.next: Pure tests reject a stale mismatched position; mounted stale-callback and other-target interaction remain open.

requirements.statement: Choices are keyed by stored value; equal translated labels remain distinct choices.
requirements.next: Mounted multi-select and chips tests select equal-label choices through distinct accessible value names and preserve stored identity across a live locale change; non-JVM interaction remains open.

requirements.statement: Each family documents autocomplete default; only true searches, explicit false overrides config true, absence behaves as false.
requirements.next: Multi-select default and local/config precedence pass pure tests; mounted local-false and true pass in both families. Chips and non-JVM interaction remain.

requirements.statement: Search filters displayed translated labels by case-insensitive substring, not stored constants.
requirements.next: Mounted multi-select and chips tests filter translated display titles after a live locale switch, rather than stored constants; non-JVM interaction remains open.

requirements.statement: No search results show a localized message; searching never creates a value.
requirements.next: Multi-select and chips no-results, localized Bulgarian empty-state and no free creation pass mounted JVM tests; non-JVM interaction remains open.

requirements.statement: options.vertical is the only choice-group orientation encoding; local value wins.
requirements.next: Three typed core cases and paired mounted radio/checkbox geometry cases pass on JVM/iOS, covering local true/false, absent option, no string alias and ignored plain global vertical. Verify RTL, physical keyboard/accessibility and browser/device rendering.

requirements.statement: Radio falls back to config.jsonformsExtended.radio.vertical then false; checkbox is local-only; global vertical and tuple vertical do not apply.
requirements.next: Nested radio default, local false precedence and checkbox local-only behavior pass typed and mounted JVM/iOS tests. Plain config.vertical is intentionally ignored; test dynamic orientation changes and RTL.

requirements.statement: False or absent orientation wraps horizontally; true stacks vertically; grouping semantics announce the drawn orientation.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM/iOS cases measure wide horizontal, narrow wrapping and vertical stacking geometry and confirm English/Bulgarian group state descriptions. Compose selectable-group semantics are present for radios and the shared checkbox renderer. Radio keyboard tests cover RTL directional navigation on JVM/iOS. Verify physical screen-reader and keyboard output, checkbox RTL geometry, and whether the JS host exposes an equivalent aria-orientation attribute.

requirements.statement: `gridColumns` and child `span` accept only positive integers.
requirements.next: Pure and mounted JVM tests cover invalid grid/span diagnostics; add platform execution and broader malformed input cases.

requirements.statement: Child `weight` is finite and greater than zero.
requirements.next: Pure JVM test covers invalid weight diagnostics; add mounted and target cases for large/invalid values.

requirements.statement: Dimensions reject inappropriate negative values and use equivalent platform logical units for numeric values.
requirements.next: Pure JVM tests cover negative and unsupported-unit diagnostics; test platform density and percentage dimensions.

requirements.statement: A child's `options.layout` controls its participation in the parent, including span, weight and size constraints.
requirements.next: Pure and mounted Material/Cupertino JVM tests cover child width/span/weight, vertical width/height bounds, and horizontal cross-axis height/min/max in ordinary, wrapped and stretched rows. Verify nested weighted containers, complex child constraints and target UI.

requirements.statement: Flat options on a layout configure its gap, wrap, alignment, justification, minimum item width and grid columns.
requirements.next: Gap/grid/defaults, wrapping, both-axis alignment and all six justifications pass mounted Material/Cupertino JVM geometry tests. Horizontal stretch fills intrinsic-capable simple children; nested SubcomposeLayout children retain natural height with layout.stretchFallback diagnostic. Verify complex controls, native/browser UI and overflow.

requirements.statement: Resolve Auto, Span, Weight and Fixed with precedence Fixed > Span > Weight > Auto.
requirements.next: Pure JVM precedence and mounted fixed/span/weight/Auto geometry pass; add vertical mode and conflict UI cases.

requirements.statement: Apply min/max as constraints rather than primary layout modes.
requirements.next: Pure and mounted JVM tests cover horizontal weighted redistribution, vertical min/max, centered vertical child width bounds, and fixed/max cross-height limits during horizontal stretch. Test horizontal overconstraints, conflicting bounds and target UI.

requirements.statement: Horizontal Auto participates in the remaining row width as weight 1.
requirements.next: Pure and mounted JVM tests cover Auto mixed with weighted/fixed/span; add equal Auto and other target interaction.

requirements.statement: Vertical Auto takes natural content height.
requirements.next: Mounted Material/Cupertino JVM scroll tests show vertical Auto and weighted controls retain natural height under indefinite height. Verify nested content and native/browser UI.

requirements.statement: Vertical weight divides only remaining height when parent height is definite or resolvable.
requirements.next: Pure resolver passes bounded and unbounded remainder allocation on JVM, iOS simulator and Wasm browser; mounted Material/Cupertino JVM tests cover bounded weighted controls and unbounded scroll. Verify nested weighted containers and native/browser UI.

requirements.statement: Column weighted children retain content-height basis; row weighted children use a zero basis.
requirements.next: Pure resolver retains unequal content bases; mounted Material/Cupertino JVM geometry confirms a 50 px difference between unequal weighted Spacer bases and the existing row width tests cover zero-basis horizontal weight. Verify weighted Group background/child stretching and target UI.

requirements.statement: Compute span width from the full logical grid: c=(W-(G-1)g)/G; spanWidth(n)=n*c+(n-1)g.
requirements.next: Pure formula with nonzero gap and mounted full-grid span geometry pass; add resizing, narrow and RTL cases.

requirements.statement: Clamp span above `gridColumns` and emit a diagnostic.
requirements.next: Pure and both-family mounted tests cover span clamp plus layout.spanClamped author diagnostic; test narrow and non-JVM cases.

requirements.statement: When row width cannot be measured, use the mathematically equivalent percentage-of-row span expression.
requirements.next: The algebraic percentage expression matches measured spans. Mounted Material/Cupertino scroll cases pass JVM, JS, Wasm and iOS with a finite window-width basis and no write; Android main compiles. Verify Android device geometry and whether narrower nested-scroll viewports need a more local percentage basis.

requirements.statement: Resolve mixed rows in order: effective children, gaps/chrome, Fixed, Span on full grid, Weight/Auto on remainder, then min/max redistribution.
requirements.next: Pure mixed-resolution math and both-family mounted geometry pass for a fitting row; add min/max, overflow and wrap geometry.

requirements.statement: Platform layout delegation for min/max redistribution is permitted only when it produces equivalent distribution.
requirements.next: The Compose adapters use the shared explicit resolver for horizontal min/max redistribution and bounded vertical weight redistribution. Focused JVM tests cover constrained mixed rows and capped columns; verify target UI geometry and resize behavior.

requirements.statement: Resolve visibility before sizing; hidden children consume no column or gap and do not enter arrangement counts.
requirements.next: Both JVM families pass hidden first/middle/last rows, nested row reflow, dynamic column reflow, live function-rule splitter divider removal and empty nested structural children; test framework placeholders and non-JVM interactions.

requirements.statement: Comments, markers, fragments and placeholders do not affect sizing, gaps or splitters.
requirements.next: Empty nested HorizontalLayout/VerticalLayout children no longer reserve a row column, column gap or splitter divider on JVM. Framework comments, fragments and placeholders are not authored Kotlin UI-schema element types; verify custom renderer no-content dispatch and other targets before claiming the full rule.

requirements.statement: Structural layouts add no implicit outer padding.
evidence: LayoutDynamicUiTest compares direct and three-level single-child nested column geometry in both Material and Cupertino on JVM; no outer gap is added
requirements.next: Verify nested Group and other structural wrappers across platforms.

requirements.statement: Apply gap only between effective visible immediate children.
requirements.next: Mounted positive Spacer row gaps, zero/config column gaps, hidden first/middle/last rows, nested single-child columns and live insertion of an empty structural child pass in both JVM families; test framework placeholders and non-JVM geometry.

requirements.statement: Ignore unsupported sizing hints with a diagnostic, including span under Group or VerticalLayout.
requirements.next: Pure and both-family mounted JVM tests cover ignored vertical span, collapsed-Group diagnostics, nested horizontal-stretch fallback and invalid options on empty root or filtered nested layouts. Expand unsupported hints and verify target UI.

requirements.statement: A boolean control-narrowing option is excluded and must draw a diagnostic; controls rely on parent layout width or maxWidth.
requirements.next: The spec describes this excluded boolean hint without naming a wire key, and the pinned React/Svelte control sources expose no matching option. Establish an actual legacy encoding before diagnosing it; do not treat arbitrary unknown renderer options as the excluded hint. Then test both families.

requirements.statement: A child integer column-count option against a fixed grid is excluded and must draw a diagnostic; use child span with configurable gridColumns.
requirements.next: Legacy child options.columns reports layout.excludedOption and leaves options.layout.span authoritative in pure JVM and focused iOS tests; mounted Material/Cupertino JVM tests verify the callback, including collapsed Groups, and editable controls. Verify browser/native UI and any additional legacy integer encoding.

requirements.statement: Any retained legacy renderer must not outrank a conforming layout renderer.
requirements.next: No legacy columns renderer is registered; a JVM registry-selection test confirms Material and Cupertino choose their conforming HorizontalLayout renderers when a child has legacy options.columns. Both registries compile on iOS, JS and Wasm. Verify selection on those targets and audit any future host-registered legacy renderer.

requirements.statement: Resolve gridColumns from local option, namespaced default, then 16.
requirements.next: Pure default/override and mounted Material/Cupertino JVM/iOS cases pass. Changing namespaced gridColumns live resizes an inherited span while a local gridColumns override remains fixed; a misplaced top-level layoutDefaults is ignored. Verify browser/Android geometry and other nested layouts.

requirements.statement: Resolve wrap from local option, namespaced default, then false and apply it.
requirements.next: Local/default/false resolution and mounted Material/Cupertino JVM/iOS cases pass. A live namespaced wrap change reflows only the inheriting row; local false keeps its row unwrapped and no data write occurs. Verify browser/Android interaction and more child types.

requirements.statement: Resolve gap from local option, namespaced default, then 16 logical units on both axes.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM geometry now confirms 20dp local, explicit zero and absent-config 16dp gaps between primitive, object and array children on both axes. Verify target density and weighted/wrapped layouts.

requirements.statement: Preserve explicit gap zero over a configured or built-in fallback.
requirements.next: Mounted Material/Cupertino ordinary row and column tests plus splitter tests prove explicit zero over the fallback. Verify target UI.

requirements.statement: Apply layout defaults even without a config object or validator-inserted schema defaults.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM tests prove the 16dp gap without a config object on both axes with primitive, object and array children. Verify non-JVM UI.

requirements.statement: Layouts own inter-child spacing and native field outer margins do not add to the layout gap.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM geometry confirms 20dp, zero and default 16dp inter-child gaps without native outer margins in column, row and wrapped-row paths. Verify weighted layouts and target UI.

requirements.statement: Container children receive the same parent gap as ordinary controls; internal control spacing remains independent.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM geometry confirms object and array controls receive the same parent gap as primitive controls in column, row and wrapped-row paths. Verify weighted layouts and target UI.

requirements.statement: Document any platform limitation with reason and observable fallback rather than changing defaults for visual preference.
requirements.next: Document proven platform limitations and test each fallback.

requirements.statement: Resolve wrapping from each child's sizing mode and minimum constraints.
requirements.next: Fit calculation covers fixed width, full-grid span and Auto/Weight minimum width in pure JVM/iOS/Wasm checks; mounted fixed/Auto cases pass. The pinned text requires resolved fit and minima, not an intrinsic-width pass for every renderer. Test mixed overconstraints, resizing and visibility.

requirements.statement: Weight and Auto children shrink before Fixed and Span when fit is constrained.
requirements.next: Pure JVM/iOS/Wasm tests show flexible width reaches its minimum before fixed width shrinks toward an authored minimum. Mounted Material/Cupertino JVM narrow-row cases show the fixed width change and preserved child order. Verify target UI and larger mixed rows.

requirements.statement: With wrap enabled, non-fitting children move to a following row.
requirements.next: Nonfitting fixed and minimum-width Auto children move to later rows in both mounted JVM families, and a 260→400 dp resize reflows three Auto children onto one row. Verify intrinsic child fit, nested content and native/browser UI.

requirements.statement: Without wrap, Span and Fixed may shrink to minima and then overflow or scroll.
requirements.next: Pure tests retain authored minima after the row becomes overconstrained. Mounted Material/Cupertino JVM tests expose horizontal scrolling for ordinary, stretch and oversized wrapped rows. Verify direct device/browser scrolling and mixed Span overflow.

requirements.statement: The parent minItemWidth supplies the default child minimum unless the child overrides it.
requirements.next: Pure fallback tests and paired Material/Cupertino mounted JVM cases pass: a parent 140dp minimum wraps at 260dp, while the second child's 60dp override returns it to the first row without a data write. The common test source compiles for JS and iOS; their runtime tests did not execute because generated test linking exhausted disk space. Verify browser/iOS/Android interaction.

requirements.statement: Auto-fit is available only when wrap is true.
requirements.next: Parent minItemWidth drives Auto line breaks only when wrap is enabled; pure no-wrap case retains one row, and both mounted JVM families reflow from two rows at 260 dp to one at 400 dp. Verify explicit auto-fit proposal semantics.

requirements.statement: Fixed children stay fixed subject to min/max constraints; flexible Span/Weight may degrade to equal shares and wrap.
requirements.next: Pure tests cover fixed minimum width and Span reduction to minimum under constraint; mounted JVM tests cover fixed-width shrink and wrap/overflow in both families. Verify Span geometry and target UI.

requirements.statement: Justify controls the main axis and align controls the cross axis.
requirements.next: Mounted Material/Cupertino JVM geometry covers horizontal and vertical justify modes, horizontal and vertical align, RTL row distribution and RTL vertical cross-axis start/center/end. Common tests compile for JS/Wasm/iOS simulator; run target UI and device interaction.

requirements.statement: Select splitter via options.variant on horizontal or vertical layout; layout type controls direction.
requirements.next: Both families select horizontal and vertical splitters in mounted JVM tests. Verify target layout direction.

requirements.statement: Initial splitter pane sizes come from normal layout sizing rather than equal shares.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM tests cover fixed, weighted and intrinsic Auto pane sizing, live natural-height changes, spare space, overconstraint scrolling, and host dimension changes. Verify iOS/browser UI and mixed min/max cases.

requirements.statement: A splitter pane span falls back to Auto with a diagnostic.
requirements.next: Span becomes Auto and reports layout.unsupportedOption through the host callback in paired mounted JVM tests. Verify vertical span and target UI.

requirements.statement: Dragged splitter sizes remain runtime state rather than authored form or UI-schema data.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM tests show user-resized shares survive host width/height changes, external data replacement and later intrinsic content growth without form or UI-schema mutation. Verify pointer drag and target UI.

requirements.statement: Vertical splitters require definite height.
requirements.next: Bounded parent height and explicit height are used; unbounded parent reports a 360dp fallback in paired JVM tests. Verify resize behavior and target layouts.

requirements.statement: Wrap with splitter is unsupported and emits a diagnostic.
requirements.next: Pure precedence and mounted Material/Cupertino JVM tests confirm splitter wrap reports layout.unsupportedOption while preserving both panes. Verify vertical splitter, global default in mounted hosts and target UI.

requirements.statement: Resizable defaults true; false keeps a visual separator without focus or dragging.
requirements.next: Default keyboard focus/resize and read-only visual divider without pointer drag or accessible resize action pass paired mounted JVM tests. Verify device/browser semantics.

requirements.statement: Hidden splitter panes leave sizing and separators.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM tests show hidden immediate panes leave sizing/separators; nested rule visibility changes intrinsic pane height, while a user-resized divider stays fixed. Verify identity and target UI.

requirements.statement: Interactive splitters support platform keyboard, focus and accessible separator semantics.
requirements.next: Horizontal and vertical keyboard resizing, focus, and accessible label pass paired mounted JVM tests. Verify touch and native/browser accessibility APIs.

requirements.statement: Spacer selects by type without schema/data binding, has intrinsic non-negative size and defaults to 32.
evidence: core UiSchemaJsonTest and LayoutSizingTest parse/default size; LayoutSpacerUiTest mounts both families without a data scope and verifies standalone fallback/invalid-size warning on JVM
requirements.next: Verify positive and unit-suffixed size values, plus non-JVM interaction.

requirements.statement: Parent resolves Spacer size on its main axis as Fixed; standalone fallback axis is height.
evidence: LayoutSpacerUiTest verifies 48-unit row width, 48-unit column height and 32-unit standalone fallback in both families on JVM
requirements.next: Verify positive gaps, explicit layout height and non-JVM geometry.

requirements.statement: Spacer participates in surrounding gap, is non-interactive/hidden to assistive technology, and never reads or writes form data.
evidence: LayoutSpacerUiTest mounts standalone and embedded Spacer in both JVM families; size updates expose no focusable/clickable/editable node and publish no onChange, while positive row gaps remain
requirements.next: Inspect platform accessibility trees and verify embedded data isolation on non-JVM targets.

requirements.statement: Spacer child weight can override intrinsic size to act as a flexible push.
evidence: LayoutSpacerUiTest verifies a zero-size weighted Spacer pushes the last row child, fills bounded column height, and retains intrinsic height in a scrolling unbounded column in Material and Cupertino on JVM
requirements.next: Verify vertical weight on Android, iOS and browser targets.

requirements.statement: Reserved child start and responsive options are accepted and ignored.
requirements.next: Both authoring UI profiles accept reserved start/responsive hints; shared sizing and diagnostics ignore them, and the demo UI-schema editor preserves them. Paired mounted JVM cases keep geometry and data unchanged through live addition of both hints. Verify non-JVM geometry.

requirements.sourceAnchor: An ordinary Group presents related controls as a labelled section.
requirements.statement: Ordinary Group is a labelled section with renderer-family default presentation and no required variant.
evidence: GroupExpansionUiTest mounts ordinary labelled, noncollapsible Groups in Material and Cupertino on JVM
requirements.next: Verify visual family presentation and target interaction.

requirements.statement: Group collapsible defaults false; true enables an accessible disclosure.
evidence: GroupExpansionUiTest opens/closes native Material TextButton and CupertinoButton disclosures with state descriptions on JVM
requirements.next: Verify keyboard and platform accessibility behavior.

requirements.sourceAnchor: | `collapsed` | `false` | Initializes expansion and synchronizes it when the effective boolean changes.
requirements.statement: Group collapsed defaults false, is ignored unless collapsible, and synchronizes on effective boolean changes.
evidence: GroupExpansionTest resolves default/local/global booleans; GroupExpansionUiTest verifies initial collapsed and effective boolean changes in both JVM families
requirements.next: Test dynamic resolver integration and more config-source transitions.

requirements.statement: Group data indicator defaults false and appears only when a bound descendant has data.
evidence: GroupExpansionTest verifies false default and local false over namespaced true; GroupDataPresenceUiTest mounts true/false options and live bound-value marker in both JVM families; GroupArrayItemContextUiTest mounts a collapsed detail Group in a real array item in both JVM families
requirements.next: Array-item Group now has paired JVM UI evidence; verify indicator on other platforms.

requirements.statement: Group validation indicator defaults false and follows §8.3 aggregation.
requirements.next: Nested array-item Group aggregation has paired JVM UI evidence; verify non-JVM interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Collapsible groups preserve field data and validation when closed.
requirements.statement: Closing a collapsible Group preserves field data and validation.
evidence: GroupExpansionUiTest closes and reopens an edited invalid field, preserving its stored value, schema error and combined validity without extra writes in both JVM families
requirements.next: Verify close/reopen and validation persistence on browser and native targets.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Data presence is defined over descendant Controls' **bound values**
requirements.statement: Data presence uses descendant Control bindings, including nested structural layouts and current array item context; unrelated data does not count.
evidence: GroupDataPresenceTest resolves nested structural Control scopes, current array-item context and literal dotted keys; GroupDataPresenceUiTest mounts root Group in both JVM families; GroupArrayItemContextUiTest mounts array-item Group with nested # scope in both JVM families
CategoryDataPresenceUiTest mounts tabs, steps and accordion in both JVM families; SpecCategorizationFixtureUiTest mounts the imported inner presentations
requirements.next: Mounted array-item Group with nested # scope passes in both JVM families; verify literal slash paths and other targets.

requirements.statement: Presence includes false and zero; missing/null, blank strings and recursively empty arrays/objects do not.
evidence: GroupDataPresenceTest checks false, zero, null, missing, whitespace-only strings and recursively empty/nonempty containers; paired JVM UI tests observe false and zero marker changes
CategoryDataPresenceUiTest observes zero, null and whitespace-only bound values with unrelated data across six JVM presentations
requirements.next: Verify nested array/object values and target interaction in live renderers.

requirements.statement: Hidden descendant Controls still contribute to structural container data presence.
evidence: GroupDataPresenceTest includes a rule-hidden Control; GroupDataPresenceUiTest shows its false value in the indicator while the Group remains collapsed and no field is mounted in both families
CategoryDataPresenceUiTest shows a hidden Control's zero value on inactive tabs, steps and closed accordion headers in both JVM families
requirements.next: Test hidden nested Group and category descendants on non-JVM targets.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The indicator means **only that data is present**.
requirements.statement: Data indicator wording must describe current data presence, not edits, validity or completion.
evidence: Both Group headers use the neutral label 'Contains data'; GroupDataPresenceUiTest verifies unrelated form data does not produce the marker in JVM Material/Cupertino
Category headers use the same neutral group.dataIndicator key; CategoryDataPresenceUiTest verifies unrelated data and blank bound values do not produce a marker
requirements.next: Review translated wording across full catalogs and visual design.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The indicator MUST carry a **localized accessible name**
requirements.statement: Data indicator has one localized string for accessible name and tooltip.
evidence: Material Badge and Cupertino marker expose a separate accessible 'group.dataIndicator' name; GroupDataPresenceUiTest verifies English-to-Bulgarian runtime update in both JVM families
CategoryDataPresenceUiTest verifies the localized status in accessible tab, step and accordion header names; SpecCategorizationFixtureUiTest checks imported English/Bulgarian text
requirements.next: Category tabs, steps and accordion now use built-in Bulgarian data-presence accessible labels without a host translator in both JVM families; verify platform accessibility trees and optional tooltip consistency.

requirements.sourceAnchor: An aggregated descendant-error indicator on a container's header.
requirements.statement: Container validation indicator is a navigation cue and does not replace inline messages.
requirements.next: Group schema inline error survives a disabled marker in both JVM families; test other containers and targets.

requirements.statement: Indicator visibility uses per-container defaults; showValidationIndicatorCount defaults false and only explicit true counts.
requirements.next: Expandable, table and list-with-detail headers, item rows, and tuple summaries verify default marker/explicit count on JVM; test grid mode and targets.

requirements.statement: Explicit local count false overrides namespaced global true; enabling indicator alone never enables counting.
requirements.next: Tuple complex summary verifies local count false over global true in both JVM families; test other container modes and targets.

requirements.statement: Aggregation collects Control and ListWithDetail scopes; nested # resolves to current context without an extra separator.
requirements.next: Nested # in an array-item Group passes in both JVM families; test mounted ListWithDetail inside inactive Category and other targets.

requirements.statement: Indicator option resolves local then namespaced global then container default; explicit false wins.
requirements.next: Expandable, table and list-with-detail headers plus tuple summaries use shared local/namespaced precedence in both JVM families; audit grid and other collection modes.

requirements.statement: Array toolbars/items and tuple complex summaries default indicator on; Group and category/tab/step headers default off.
requirements.next: Expandable, table and list-with-detail headers, item rows, and tuple complex summaries default on in JVM tests; audit grid and other targets.

requirements.sourceAnchor: **Applicability.** Any container that renders a header
requirements.statement: Indicator applies to header-bearing containers, never ordinary Controls or headerless layouts; no header is added to show it.
requirements.next: Check other headerless layouts and ordinary Controls.

requirements.sourceAnchor: **What belongs to a container.** An error belongs
requirements.statement: Membership uses normalized instance-path segments, not textual prefixes; structural containers use descendant bound scopes and mapped host errors.
requirements.next: Mounted array-item Group host path passes in both JVM families, and core array grouping separates rows 1 and 10 and escaped pointer segments; test mounted escaped paths and other targets.

requirements.sourceAnchor: **Setting it to `false` hides only the aggregated indicator.**
requirements.statement: Disabling aggregate indicator leaves own/field errors, validation, validity, guards and data unchanged.
requirements.next: Group field errors/validity, expandable/table/list own errors, expandable/table delete guards and tuple position-owned errors survive marker suppression in JVM tests. Audit grid and other targets.

requirements.statement: Hidden descendants retain eligible errors in container aggregation.
requirements.next: Add Category coverage and non-JVM interaction evidence.

requirements.statement: Indicator follows validation display policy; hidden schema errors stay hidden while host errors remain.
requirements.next: Check target execution and own-error presentation across modes.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The indicator summarizes displayable section errors independently
requirements.statement: Section indicator may appear before touch; explicit count ignores descendant pre-touch text filtering.
requirements.next: With opt-in required-keyword filtering, Material/Cupertino JVM tests cover untouched required text, enum, oneOf, editable anyOf, checkbox, toggle, radio, oneOf radio and slider with an unchanged section count; text blur reveal and immediate nonmatching same-field host error. Default-off clear tests show required feedback after clearing a selected enum/oneOf. Checkbox interaction replaces hidden required feedback with visible const feedback in both JVM families. Enum-array selection clears its hidden required error; existing minItems remains inline in paired JVM tests. Verify choice blur/dismissal, other discrete interactions, file/null extended controls, target interaction and accessibility.

requirements.sourceAnchor: A locale change refreshes the accessible name
requirements.statement: Locale change updates indicator accessible name and count without data edit.
requirements.next: Group, Category, array summary/item, tuple position, table composite cell, row-detail and page-error indicators now use English/Bulgarian built-in labels. Live Bulgarian switching passes mounted JVM Material/Cupertino cases with no writes and stable host override keys. Test all table variants and browser/native accessibility.

requirements.statement: Array summary hide option suppresses child aggregate even if show indicator true, but preserves own array error explanation.
requirements.next: Expandable, table and list-with-detail hide requests preserve own minItems explanation in Material/Cupertino JVM; test grid mode and target interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Compact object and array cells MUST expose eligible errors
requirements.statement: Closed compact object/array cells expose value and descendant errors beside summary independently of outer header indicator.
requirements.next: Exercise object/array cells on target UI, audit other registered cells and verify nested errors across additional collection variants.

requirements.statement: Composed object cells include composition-level and descendant errors; details use ordinary registry dispatch.
requirements.next: Check composed-cell target UI, mixed-type array alternatives and error policy variants.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Keep the summary or scalar editor and its error indicator on the same line.
requirements.statement: Compact cell summary/editor and error indicator stay on one line with reserved space.
requirements.next: Test additional scalar/registered cell kinds, AG Grid hosting and target accessibility at narrow widths.

requirements.sourceAnchor: **Never scan the error list per container.**
requirements.statement: Container presence lookup must use a shared ancestor index rather than per-container error scans.
requirements.next: A 242-container JVM sample favors indexed counts at 200 and 1000 errors; audit remaining collection paths and target performance.

requirements.sourceAnchor: **Build an ancestor index once per validation.**
requirements.statement: Build ancestor prefixes from normalized error instance paths once per validation and share across containers.
requirements.next: Reference-key cache and two mounted Group renderers share one provider index on JVM; verify browser/device provider interaction and retained-index lifetime.

requirements.statement: Scope-less bound descendant paths are collected once by UI-schema identity for presence and validation indicators.
requirements.next: Category headers now share one remembered bound-scope traversal and pass replacement tests; verify native target interaction and audit other scope-less containers.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Runtime expansion MUST NOT mutate the UI schema.
requirements.statement: Expansion initializes from collapsed and synchronizes on effective boolean changes without mutating authored UI schema.
evidence: GroupExpansionUiTest initializes from collapsed and synchronizes on effective boolean changes in both JVM families; renderer stores expansion in Compose state
requirements.next: Assert UI-schema immutability and dynamic source behavior across targets.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Unrelated re-renders, or replacement UI elements
requirements.statement: Unrelated rerenders and equal effective booleans preserve local expansion; header interaction never writes source property.
evidence: GroupExpansionUiTest preserves local expansion through replacement UI elements, host data replacement and unrelated config changes, then responds to a changed effective collapsed boolean without writes in both JVM families
requirements.next: Test one-way dynamic source semantics and non-JVM interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Undefined resolution falls back to the ordinary static value
requirements.statement: Undefined collapsed falls back to static/default false; nonboolean including null diagnoses without truthiness coercion.
evidence: GroupExpansionTest rejects null, string and numeric collapsed values without truthiness; GroupExpansionUiTest receives section.invalidCollapsed on null in both JVM families
requirements.next: Test undefined dynamic fallback, string diagnostics and disabling dynamic resolution.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Ordinary Categorization selects tabs without a variant.
requirements.statement: Categorization defaults to tabs; stepper and accordion are explicit variants.
requirements.next: Tabs, stepper and accordion now render in both JVM families; verify variant selection and interaction on native/browser targets.

requirements.statement: Stepper nav buttons default false; vertical and initial options follow the §8.6 table.
requirements.next: Four paired JVM geometry/interaction scenarios verify vertical tabs and steps at 600 and 320 dp; core rejects string/legacy orientation encodings. Check long translations and target accessibility.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Previous and Next operate on **visible** categories
requirements.statement: Previous/Next stop at visible bounds; hide does not leave selection invalid; actions change runtime selection only and require no validation gate.
requirements.next: Mounted Material/Cupertino tabs and steps pass removal, reorder and orientation-change selection tests on JVM; test UI-schema immutability and native target interaction.

requirements.statement: Initial selects direct named Category; missing target diagnoses and falls back to first visible; sibling names should be unique.
requirements.next: Test duplicate sibling names, hidden initial target on a live form, and target execution.

requirements.sourceAnchor: A container's own visibility follows its rule
requirements.statement: Container visibility uses own rule/context, hidden ancestor suppresses subtree, child rule only hides child.
requirements.next: Function-rule path/config now reaches control, category and mounted layout visibility on JVM; test hidden ancestor suppression, Group/Category child-only rules and non-JVM interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Hidden immediate children consume no layout space
requirements.statement: Visible Group/Category retains heading and navigation entry when all children hidden, without implicit hide-when-empty.
requirements.next: Exercise empty visible Group and Category on device/browser targets and cover nested category variants.

requirements.sourceAnchor: When the selected category becomes hidden
requirements.statement: On selected-category hide/removal select visible fallback; empty eligible set has no active panel; visible empty category remains selectable.
requirements.next: Test category removal/reorder, visible empty category, and non-JVM execution.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Matches a Categorization with direct Category children
requirements.statement: Accordion tester requires direct Categories and explicit variant, outranks generic category and needs no data scope/schema type.
requirements.next: Explicit variant outranks generic in mounted Material/Cupertino forms; test unbound empty-data rendering on native targets.

requirements.sourceAnchor: **At most one visible category is open.**
requirements.statement: Accordion opens at most one visible panel; toggling open header closes it; explicit all-closed state survives unrelated updates.
requirements.next: Mounted Material/Cupertino pointer and rerender behavior passes; state description and semantic click pass on JVM. Check keyboard and accessibility on native targets.

requirements.sourceAnchor: an active category becomes hidden or is removed
requirements.statement: Accordion falls back to first visible after active hide/removal and preserves identity across reordering.
requirements.next: Mounted Material/Cupertino hide, removal, duplicate names, reorder and all-hidden recovery pass on JVM; verify native target interaction.

requirements.statement: Accordion initial selection is mount-only; runtime expansion changes neither data nor UI schema and closed content retains data/validation.
requirements.next: Mounted Material/Cupertino initial, close, unrelated data rerender and closed-panel validation pass with no data changes; test UI schema identity and native target interaction.

requirements.statement: Accordion collapsed resolves local then global default false; initial overrides mount collapse; effective changes synchronize without unrelated reset.
requirements.next: Core option precedence and mounted Material/Cupertino local false, global change and initial override pass; test dynamic resolution and native target interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Mixed object/array outer frames use the same
requirements.statement: Mixed frames use Group collapsible/collapsed precedence; default collapsible/expanded; noncollapsible stays open.
requirements.next: Focused core precedence and Material/Cupertino mounted default, toggle, option changes, noncollapsible, and invalid-value diagnostic pass on JVM; test nested mixed detail contexts and native target interaction.

requirements.statement: Accordion orientation and stepper-only showNavButtons do not change stacked panel presentation.
requirements.next: Two paired JVM geometry scenarios confirm stacked panels and absent step navigation with vertical/showNavButtons; verify native target interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Defaults when extension config is absent
requirements.statement: The namespaced URL policy defaults to https/http/mailto, relative URLs allowed and image data URLs refused; configured members override defaults independently.
requirements.next: Link, ImageView and Markdown call the shared policy; verify actual navigation/image rendering and policy changes on browser and native targets.

requirements.statement: Restrict resolves from the element option, then authored host config, then true; explicit false disables preventive editing constraints without disabling validation.
requirements.next: Compose renderers now resolve authored option and config before the true default. Paired JVM tests cover array and additional-property minimum guards plus explicit local false. Verify all supported controls and native/browser interactions, and ensure non-Compose hosts resolve before core seeds its false default.

requirements.statement: URL-template data, item and locale substitutions are component encoded before the final URL passes policy.
requirements.next: Markdown Label textParams now percent-encode UTF-8 data/item/locale substitutions inside inline and reference-style link destinations, including parentheses, before the existing Markdown URL policy check. The 51 pure and 36 mounted cases pass on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm with reserved characters, Bulgarian Unicode, live data/locale replacement, safe prose/titles and refused authored schemes. Verify other URL-template hosts.

requirements.sourceAnchor: A declared flag must be consulted
requirements.statement: Image data URLs need allowImageDataUrls and an image MIME type even when data is an allowed scheme; host policy may narrow further.
requirements.next: Direct ImageView source opt-in and image MIME tests pass on JVM; add scoped image-data and cross-target rendering checks.

requirements.sourceAnchor: At least one of `src` or `scope` MUST be supplied
requirements.statement: ImageView requires alt and src or scope, keeps defined empty src and decorative empty alt, resolves scoped strings without coercion, and applies URL policy to every source.
requirements.next: Direct/empty/refused source precedence, scoped array-item strings, URL policy and both mounted renderer families have JVM evidence. Verify dynamic overlay sources and mounted iOS/JS/Wasm behavior.

requirements.statement: Separator is a static display-only horizontal or vertical divider with native visuals and accessible orientation; it does not read or change form data.
requirements.next: Typed parsing, native Material/Cupertino dividers, row geometry, localized semantics, no-action behavior, rule visibility and invalid vertical-option diagnostics pass paired JVM tests; verify native target accessibility and orientation behavior in nested layouts.

requirements.statement: Link preserves empty href as non-navigating text, applies URL policy to every destination and enforces noopener for a blank target.
requirements.next: Paired JVM UI tests cover safe/inert URLs, tightened policy, locale changes and invalid target; rel normalization adds noopener and noreferrer. The installed Compose UI API has no Link role, so the navigable control retains native button semantics. Verify browser/native navigation, accessibility treatment and imported fixture behavior.

requirements.statement: Template resolves the first registry UI schema with an exact case-sensitive top-level name, without invoking ranked testers.
requirements.next: Test missing name and case-sensitive lookup through both live renderer families.

requirements.statement: Duplicate names and missing templates produce diagnostics; a missing template renders no substituted content.
requirements.next: Assert diagnostic delivery and empty substitution in Compose UI tests.

requirements.statement: Named slot content overrides inherited content, later same-name children win, and unnamed children do not fill slots.
requirements.next: Test duplicate local slot names and unnamed children through live rendering.

requirements.statement: An unfilled Slot renders only its first fallback child, or nothing when no fallback exists.
requirements.next: Add a live UI test with multiple fallback children and an empty Slot.

requirements.statement: Named reuse preserves the caller schema and data path; edits update caller data.
requirements.next: Verify nested path and rule/validation context on other target runners.

requirements.statement: Recursive named references are guarded against unbounded expansion.
requirements.next: Test slot recursion and both renderer families across supported targets.

requirements.statement: Template name lookup remains distinct from ranked UI-schema selection used by details and branches.
requirements.next: Add interaction tests where registry entries have high-ranked testers and duplicate names.

requirements.statement: TemplateLayout chooses explicit lang, then configured default, then the default web profile; unknown or unsupported languages are diagnosed rather than silently mapped to another engine.
requirements.next: The unsupported fallback distinguishes language, policy and unavailable-engine cases. Both development and production Web Component bundles show template.engineUnavailable with a visible JSX notice under explicit script permission in Chrome, without a data write. A real web engine still needs a DOM island, cleanup proof, delegated-child tests and a separate browser registry.

requirements.statement: A TemplateLayout engine exposes whole-form data, core schema errors, context, child elements and translate as distinct engine bindings.
requirements.next: Implement a disposable DOM template host and expose the specified bindings; test each binding in a browser.

requirements.statement: Live data, schema-error and context changes refresh TemplateLayout bindings without leaving stale slot editors.
requirements.next: Prove delegated-child lifecycle and test live data, error and context changes in a browser engine.

requirements.statement: TemplateLayout's core schema errors binding must not be presented as combined form validity.
requirements.next: Keep schema errors distinct from additional and renderer-owned errors when a browser engine is added; test validity messaging.

requirements.statement: An unnamed TemplateLayout child receives an index fallback only if that name does not collide with an explicit child name.
requirements.next: Define collision-safe child addressing in the browser adapter and test an explicit numeric name beside an unnamed child.
