requirements.statement: A TemplateLayout child that cannot be addressed by the template is reported rather than silently omitted.
requirements.next: Report inaccessible child names with an author diagnostic in a browser engine and test it.

requirements.statement: TemplateLayout placeholders resolve to the authored child UI-schema element and delegate it at its original schema and data path.
requirements.next: Prove a DOM island can mount a delegated Compose child at its original path before adding a template engine.

requirements.statement: Template-local UI state must not become committed form data.
requirements.next: The fallback does not dispatch changes; prove template-local state isolation once a browser engine exists.

requirements.statement: Executable TemplateLayout profiles follow host trust policy and require independent script-evaluation permission; enabling $dynamic alone does not grant it.
requirements.next: The fallback checks explicit allowScriptEvaluation and never executes a template; verify trust and independent $dynamic permission in a real browser engine.

requirements.statement: Each TemplateLayout engine documents its expression, event, raw-HTML and data-write capabilities.
requirements.next: Publish a capability contract for any added browser engine before enabling its renderer.

requirements.statement: TemplateLayout engine two-way binding cannot bypass read-only, restrict or normal change dispatch.
requirements.next: Route delegated edits through shared dispatch with mutation guards and test read-only and restrict changes.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The action, script, label, icon, color and params fields are top-level fields
requirements.statement: Button action, script, label, icon, color and params are top-level fields; options is not an alias for them.
requirements.next: Action, label and icon option aliases are ignored in mounted tests; the webcomponent event preserves an authored Button rule and extension field. Cover malformed top-level fields, icon-only labels, and full semantic-color visual checks on remaining targets.

requirements.statement: When a Button has both action and script, dispatch action and report the authoring conflict.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM and JS browser cases pass; verify iOS simulator and Wasm browser interaction.

requirements.statement: An absent action and script selects the stable element name, or an empty action identifier when unnamed; an explicit script takes precedence over name.
requirements.next: Script-only buttons take precedence over stable names and run through an opt-in browser executor when trusted; native hosts without an executor retain the unsupported diagnostic. Verify malformed fields and Android behavior.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Colour names are semantic, not literal
requirements.statement: The six portable Button color names map through each renderer family's theme palette rather than being treated as literal colors.
requirements.next: Verify warning, alternative, secondary and success appearance in light/dark themes, and mounted color output on iOS, JS, Wasm and Android.

requirements.statement: Button remains a command control with native button semantics, keyboard activation, disabled and pending behavior; styling it like a link must not turn its action into navigation.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM and JS browser cases verify native Button role, focus, Enter/Space activation, disabled keys and local/form read-only transitions; verify keyboard and pending behavior on iOS, Wasm and Android.

requirements.statement: Button action dispatch awaits handler completion, disables and synchronously guards duplicate activation while pending, then clears pending and propagates handler rejection.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM, JS browser, Wasm browser and iOS simulator tests cover event payload/context snapshots, callback precedence, pending state and duplicate activation; the legacy callback remains compatible. A mounted Chrome custom-element test covers event payload, waitUntil completion, duplicate suppression, rejection reporting and subsequent recovery. A missing host handler now leaves the Button pressable, clears pending and reports action.unhandled once when a reporter exists, with JVM tests for late reporter/handler installation. Verify that path on other targets, visual indicator appearance and Android interaction.

requirements.statement: Button options.fullWidth defaults false and fills only its containing layout cell when true; intrinsic sizing remains for false or absent, without changing the cell allocation or treating block as an alias.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM/JS browser cases reject string-valued fullWidth. Paired mounted Material/Cupertino JVM and iOS simulator tests verify that fullWidth fills its allocated one-column grid or one-weight flex cell without changing cell allocation or the neighboring three-column/three-weight cell and Button. A focused Wasm browser run stalled without a result; verify Wasm interaction.

requirements.statement: A string Button script runs only with explicit security.allowScriptEvaluation, as an async function body bound to the action event; pending and duplicate guards cover completion, and CSP refusal is diagnosed without bypassing policy.
requirements.applicability: web-only with portable host executor contract
requirements.next: JVM, JS, iOS and Wasm mounted tests cover the trust gate and host executor; mounted Chrome covers top-level await, this bindings, pending, duplicate suppression, rejection, recovery and a restrictive CSP that blocks evaluation with a diagnostic. Verify Android host behavior and CSP response-header deployment; the webcomponent uses the custom-element host as $el.

requirements.sourceAnchor: A function-valued script is a build-time convenience outside the wire format
requirements.statement: A platform may accept a function-valued Button script; if accepted, it receives the event as both an argument and this, and does not require string-evaluation permission.
requirements.next: The Kotlin Button contract accepts a JSON string script through an explicit host executor, not a function-valued script. No function bridge is claimed for commonMain or the webcomponent. If one is added, test event argument/this equivalence and independent permission behavior.

requirements.sourceAnchor: A function-valued script MUST NOT be stringified
requirements.statement: A platform accepting a function-valued Button script must invoke the callback, never stringify it into an async body.
requirements.next: No function-valued script API exists; the current string handler receives only a JSON string. Keep this prohibition as an adoption gate for any future browser or host callback bridge.

requirements.statement: Shared confirmation resolves element, renderer, global and fallback policy in order; complex examines discarded old values and always treats false, zero, empty strings and containers as present.
requirements.next: Add cross-family tests for every covered operation and all falsey/empty values.

requirements.statement: Additional-property deletion uses catalog ID additionalProperties and the shared delete policy; native dialog cancellation preserves data, and confirmation rechecks permission and target.
requirements.next: Test policy overrides, restriction bounds, translated dialogs and non-JVM targets.

requirements.statement: Array, tuple-tail, tree, mixed type, combinator branch and composite-cell destructive operations share confirmation without stale callbacks, preserving data and selection on cancellation.
requirements.next: Verify oneOf Clear focus/hover-only affordance and keyboard activation, type/branch prompt focus on devices, and remaining stale/restrict cases. Generic anyOf tabs are view navigation and do not invoke branchChange.

requirements.statement: Form-wide readonly wins; applicable read-only rules then UI options, config, schema readOnly and inherited renderer state decide readonly in order, with earlier false values overriding later sources.
requirements.next: Core and mounted Material/Cupertino tests cover readonly rules and strict Boolean inputs. Cell mapping invokes the shared resolver even with own readonly false; focused JVM/iOS and full core JS/Wasm suites pass. Android main compiles; verify Android runtime and remaining renderer mutation paths.

requirements.statement: With separateReadonlyFromDisabled false, readonly disables controls; with true, effective readonly and enabled state remain distinct and mutations stay guarded.
requirements.next: Material and Cupertino text fields support enabled but read-only inspection in mounted JVM and focused iOS simulator tests; audit other controls and JS, Wasm and Android targets.

requirements.statement: A renderer family that cannot fully separate read-only from disabled state declares the capability unsupported.
requirements.next: Both families declare partial text-field support and unsupported family-wide separation; finish control-by-control interaction and accessibility tests before advertising full support.

requirements.statement: Schema-based UI rules evaluate form data independently of collected additional errors, pending editor validation and the automatic validation mode.
requirements.next: Mounted Material/Cupertino JVM and iOS simulator tests cover NoValidation, host-error changes, data-driven visibility, temporal picker disposal and invalid-draft pending cleanup when hidden. JVM tests also confirm the rule remains visible during the pending draft. Verify other rule effects, JS, Wasm and Android.

requirements.statement: A host command guard requiring a valid form uses combined validity, including additional errors and pending work, rather than schema-rule evaluation.
requirements.next: A mounted host Submit command uses onValidityChange and rejects host additional errors, schema errors, renderer pending edits and NoValidation; paired Material/Cupertino tests pass on JVM and iOS simulator. Verify JS, Wasm and Android host integration.

requirements.statement: Schema conditional-validation keywords do not create UI visibility rules; conditional presentation requires an explicit UI rule.
requirements.next: Eight mounted Material/Cupertino tests cover if/then, else and dependentRequired validation without inferred visibility; all pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser. Verify Android interaction and additional dependency dialects.

requirements.statement: Cached combined validity distinguishes unvalidated, pending, stale, valid and invalid; NoValidation's empty schema-error list does not prove validity and ValidateAndHide retains hidden failures.
requirements.next: JVM and focused iOS simulator tests cover statuses, hidden failures and unvalidated transitions; verify all renderer consumers and JS, Wasm and Android.

requirements.statement: Validation-mode changes update presentation and notify integrations without a data edit.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM and focused iOS simulator tests cover callback changes; Group presentation has paired JVM evidence. Verify other family presentations and JS, Wasm and Android.

requirements.statement: Restrict and mutation or action permissions remain independent of validation mode, and restrict false does not disable schema validation.
requirements.next: Mounted Material/Cupertino JVM and iOS simulator tests cover maxLength and array min/max prevention under NoValidation, local restrict false, revalidation on mode change, and Button read-only/disabled action permissions. Verify other controls and JS/Wasm/Android.

requirements.statement: Complete host validity uses schema results, host and renderer additional errors and participating pending work rather than presentation-filtered or translated error text.
requirements.next: Core and mounted JVM plus focused iOS simulator tests cover combined status; verify host command guards, presentation independence and JS, Wasm and Android.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Notify combined-validity consumers when additional errors or pending state
requirements.statement: Combined-validity consumers are notified when additional errors, pending work or validation mode change without a data edit.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM and focused iOS simulator callback tests cover status, pending, mode and same-count error replacement; verify JS, Wasm and Android callbacks.

requirements.statement: When an editor's logical target moves, relocate only its published error paths; deleting that owner clears its errors.
requirements.next: A real table file-size diagnostic follows its row on reorder while host errors stay at their original path. Audit other array reorder/delete integrations, filtered rows and async target disposal.

requirements.statement: Editor ownership is based on stable logical identity rather than only an array index or display label.
requirements.next: Portable table rows now use occurrence IDs through field edits and authored moves, including duplicate row references. Audit other row renderers, external replacement and filtering.

requirements.statement: Moving or clearing renderer-owned errors does not rewrite or erase host-supplied error paths.
requirements.next: Mounted table test confirms the host error remains at row 0 while the file renderer's size error moves to row 1. Verify other owner types and external data replacement.

requirements.statement: Participating async validation remains pending during owner reassociation; stale old-target results cannot establish validity or publish at the wrong path.
requirements.next: Controller tests cover moved-request path rejection and pending validity. Mounted Material/Cupertino JVM and iOS simulator file-cell tests show that a pending picker blocks row moves, then resolving it permits a move and rejects a late callback. External host replacement also retires event and legacy picker callbacks at an unchanged field value. Verify pending owner reassociation from other hosts and repeat mounted cases on JS, Wasm and Android.

requirements.statement: Schema constraints and registered custom formats use normal schema validation; controls do not republish them as additional errors.
requirements.next: Ten mounted Material/Cupertino duration, cron, date, time and date-time cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser. Temporal range errors use the schema channel only, including after host error replacement; audit remaining registered custom formats and renderer publication paths.

requirements.statement: Renderer diagnostic publication is opt-in per element/config and disabling it preserves schema and application errors.
requirements.next: File-size publication defaults off and resolves strict Boolean `propagateErrors` from Control then namespaced config. Mounted Material/Cupertino cases verify local feedback, opt-out, toggling and host/schema preservation on JVM, iOS, JS and Wasm. Audit other publishing renderers and the missing-integration diagnostic.

requirements.statement: Every renderer-published error has a stable instance owner; clearing one owner preserves other owners and host errors.
requirements.next: Two real file controls at one path preserve independent size errors and the host error through disposal and size-option changes on JVM, iOS, JS and Wasm. Audit other diagnostic-producing renderers and owner identity under row reorders.

requirements.statement: An owner's errors clear when its subject changes and remain correctly merged when the host replaces the error collection.
requirements.next: File size errors survive host error-list replacement and layout-only changes, then clear on disposal or file replacement on JVM, iOS, JS and Wasm. New mounted JVM/iOS tests show external data-subject replacement retires pending picker state and measured-size knowledge even at the same path/value. Verify other async renderer requests and row reorders on JS, Wasm and Android.

requirements.statement: Publication reaches form validity immediately and never replays a stale data snapshot.
requirements.next: Live file size publication changes combined validity without stale host data, with controlled host echo on JVM, iOS, JS and Wasm. New mounted JVM/iOS tests reject late event and legacy picker callbacks after external subject replacement. Audit remaining publishing renderers and async stale-result paths on JS, Wasm and Android.

requirements.statement: A publishing renderer reports a diagnostic when no form-level additional-error integration exists.
requirements.applicability: conditional; missing integration is unreachable through the supported Kotlin JsonForms host
requirements.next: JsonForms always enters JsonFormsStateProvider, which creates an owned additional-error store and supplies its non-null controller through LocalJsonFormsContext before dispatching any renderer. File publishing uses that controller; it has no optional host integration flag. Focused Compose controller tests (13) and paired Material/Cupertino file-publication tests (2) pass on JVM without a host additionalErrors input. Direct renderer composition outside JsonFormsStateProvider is outside the supported host API and throws for missing context rather than silently dropping publication. Reassess if a standalone renderer host becomes supported.

requirements.statement: Pre-touch filtering defaults off; when enabled, an absent or empty keyword array suppresses all otherwise displayable inline Control error text, while a non-empty array suppresses only matching keywords.
requirements.next: Verify malformed keyword diagnostics, runtime config changes and all renderer roles on every target.

requirements.statement: Receiving focus alone does not mark a Control touched; leaving it does, even without a data edit. Touch remains runtime state.
requirements.next: Text blur is exercised on JVM; verify discrete focus-group blur, menu dismissal, owner reset and non-JVM interaction.

requirements.statement: Filtering changes only inline presentation; structured errors, validation, form validity, data and rule semantics remain intact, and disabling filtering restores display subject to validation mode.
requirements.next: JVM tests preserve Invalid and zero data changes; add live mode/config toggles, rule consumer and target execution.

requirements.statement: Filter the complete mapped inline error set, including matching additional errors, while retaining non-matching additional errors and their validity contribution.
requirements.next: Verify multiple translated additional-error owners, host replacement and non-JVM behavior.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Pre-touch filtering applies to inline Control error text
requirements.statement: Group and Category indicators summarize displayable structured errors independently of Control touch state.
requirements.next: JVM Group counts are covered; test Category under opt-in filtering and target accessibility.

requirements.statement: Restricted string input prevents excess maxLength entry using the displayed-to-stored representation, while explicit false permits invalid commits for validation feedback.
requirements.next: Single-line/multiline Material and Cupertino text and Material anyOf text guard Unicode code-point length; paired JVM tests cover restricted edits and explicit false committing an overlong string with Invalid combined validity. Verify other string formats and native/browser interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Already-invalid data must remain visible and repairable
requirements.statement: Already-invalid values stay visible without mount mutation, and edits toward validity remain possible under restriction.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM text inputs preserve overlong external data and accept shortening edits while rejecting growth. Enum-array checkbox tests repair under-minimum and duplicate over-maximum values one occurrence at a time. Material/Cupertino multi-select tests preserve and repair arrays imported above maxItems or below minItems. Table/expandable arrays visibly preserve numeric/null imports and distinguish a missing field; mounted JVM/iOS tests repair all three with Add. Both tuple families visibly preserve a non-array import and repair it through fixed-position editing, with English/Bulgarian labels and English fallback. Verify remaining array/property repair paths and mounted JS/Wasm/Android interactions.

requirements.statement: Restricted checkbox groups enforce minItems and maxItems on visible choices and the mutation handler using resulting array size.
requirements.next: Paired Material/Cupertino JVM tests cover checkbox boundaries, local false and repair; Cupertino still delegates to the Material checkbox renderer. Multi-select and chips are now implemented in both families with shared count guards; focused multi-select repair passes on JVM/iOS. Verify browser/device interaction and remaining batch edits.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Evaluate batch edits against their resulting size
requirements.statement: Under restrict, array additions and removals use the resulting minItems/maxItems count in action state and mutation handlers; count-preserving replacements remain allowed, and already-invalid arrays can move toward validity.
requirements.next: Shared count checks permit same-size replacements and moves toward validity. Material/Cupertino multi-select UI cases repair imported over-maximum and under-minimum arrays on JVM/iOS without mount writes. Finite choices now expose a count-preserving Replace action at minItems, maxItems and equal-bound cardinality in both families; guarded updates reject stale or duplicate targets. All 22 mounted multi-select tests pass on JVM/iOS, including both boundary swaps, external replacement closing its menu, live Bulgarian text and English fallback for an unsupported German tag. Ordinary table/expandable Add now rechecks the snapshot and maximum in its updater; 12 mounted JVM/iOS cases cover min/max transitions, local false, visible invalid imports and missing/null repair, and the shared helper passes on JVM/iOS/JS Node/Wasm browser. Verify keyboard handler guards, other array families and mounted JS/Wasm/Android interaction.

requirements.statement: Renderer-owned add, remove, move, clear and replacement actions obey the current read-only and enabled state, including when state changes while an action menu is open.
requirements.next: Paired JVM/iOS cases show read-only and DISABLE transitions close pending Replace and Add menus without changing data; restoring edit permission leaves the menus closed until reopened. The shared chips renderer also passes 14 JVM cases. Verify other mutation actions, direct handler guards and JS/Wasm/Android interaction.

requirements.statement: Restricted property counts govern add and remove across declared and dynamic keys but do not prevent a count-preserving rename; name and value rules still apply, and stale renames cannot overwrite newer host data.
requirements.next: Material/Cupertino mounted JVM/iOS cases rename a dynamic property with minProperties = maxProperties = 2 while add/delete are disabled, and close pending drafts on read-only or host-data changes. Four mounted Material/Cupertino cases pass on JVM/iOS: a rename preserves count at the equal boundary, Add repairs an under-minimum object counting the declared field, and local restrict:false permits an over-maximum commit with Invalid validity. Six shared tests pass on JVM/iOS/JS Node/Wasm browser, including stale Add/rename rejection and name collisions. Verify disabled-rule transitions, mounted JS/Wasm/Android interaction and other property editor paths.

requirements.statement: Renderer profiles declare the exact constraints and interaction paths with preventive support, distinguish validation-only behavior, and retain validation for external and unsupported data.
requirements.next: The §15.8 matrix inventories arrays, tuple tails, checkbox groups, multi-selects/chips, additional properties, text, numeric, temporal and file paths with explicit handler and target gaps. Expand to every renderer catalog entry and verify remaining stale callback, keyboard, native picker and browser/device paths before claiming full compliance.

requirements.statement: Automatic enum-array checkbox selection prevents restricted count violations while preserving invalid incoming values and permitting repair.
requirements.next: Twenty-four mounted checkbox cases pass on JVM/iOS across both families, covering bounds, duplicate-occurrence repair, imported values outside the checkbox options, and local-only horizontal/wrapped/vertical orientation with English/Bulgarian group semantics. Unknown array entries display their JSON value and can be removed one occurrence at a time under the same restricted count guard; a non-array import remains visible until explicit choice selection. Missing data does not display as imported null. Native Cupertino presentation and browser/device checkbox interaction remain open.

requirements.statement: Explicit multi-select applies only to finite unique string arrays, stores chosen values rather than labels, blocks free entry and duplicate additions, and obeys restricted count boundaries.
requirements.next: Pure core tests execute on JVM, JS browser or Node, Wasm browser and iOS simulator; mounted JVM and earlier JS browser cases cover both families, restrictions, live translated labels/search, invalid imports, repair, positional removal names, equal-label selection accessibility and all imported fixture categories. Finite imported unknown items now show a localized out-of-domain marker with their JSON text, without a mount or locale-change write; mounted Material/Cupertino cases cover the marker and removal. Six newer mounted cases verify repair from over-maximum and under-minimum imports and fixed-count choice replacement on JVM and iOS. The replacement helper also passes focused JS Node and Wasm browser tests; updated UI sources compile on both. Verify new browser/Android interactions and device accessibility.

requirements.statement: Explicit chips support finite string choices or free string tokens, preserve duplicates when uniqueItems is absent, remove the acted-on occurrence and enforce restricted array counts.
requirements.next: Pure core tests execute on JVM, JS browser, Wasm browser and iOS simulator; paired mounted JVM and JS browser cases cover draft commit, duplicate removal with positional accessibility names, finite labels with distinct accessible value names, restricted counts, readonly, live locale search and all imported fixture categories. Paired mounted finite-chip cases show an imported numeric item as actual JSON text with an out-of-domain marker, preserve it on mount, then remove only that occurrence. Verify Wasm/iOS/Android renderer interaction and device accessibility.

requirements.statement: Declared tuple positions have no Add, Delete or Reorder action; equal bounds alone do not change a uniform array into a positional tuple.
requirements.next: Test nested-position scope behavior, omitted-position error summary, border appearance and accessibility, then complete fixture interactions on all targets.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Render all declared fields even when data is missing
requirements.statement: Missing tuple positions render without changing data; editing a later position initializes unambiguous preceding positions and commits the prefix and edit together without sparse or null padding.
requirements.next: Retain ambiguous-prefix edits as local drafts with position feedback; cover nested authored scopes, rapid updates, explicit defaults, and native platform interactions.

requirements.sourceAnchor: An inline `options.detail` layout on a tuple arranges its fixed positions.
requirements.statement: Inline tuple options.detail layouts arrange fixed positions through ordinary layout semantics; whole-position controls preserve their own labels and scopes, and invalid position scopes produce diagnostics.
requirements.next: Test rule-hidden position summaries in nested layouts, authored-layout visibility/sizing and cyclic registry delegation across platforms; current JVM evidence covers multi-position indexing and ValidateAndHide.

requirements.statement: Complex tuple positions use compact summaries and an edit dialog with ranked detail resolution, committed-draft semantics and discoverable errors.
requirements.next: Test complete validator direct/descendant error placement, rapid pending input, nested drafts, focus and non-JVM interactions.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Disable Empty contents when the value is absent or already empty
requirements.statement: Tuple complex-position Clear preserves the fixed slot and is disabled for absent, empty, readonly, disabled or disableRemove states; under restrict it also guards required, minProperties, minItems and positive contains minima using the position schema.
requirements.next: Ninety-five mounted tuple cases pass on JVM, including paired Material/Cupertino positive-contains, boolean contains, composed allOf minimum, live restrict and disableRemove cases; shared source compiles for JS/Wasm/iOS simulator. Core structural and active-validator tests cover required/minProperties/minItems/contains, boolean contains, minContains zero and composed object/array minima; seven focused cases pass on JVM and JS Node. Run the new mounted cases on non-JVM targets and verify local position-option precedence, physical input and stale callbacks.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Apply the shared validation and pending-edit contracts to tuple fields
requirements.statement: Tuple array, position and nested errors remain at their respective scopes; complex positions expose an accessible closed-summary error indicator for validator and additional errors.
requirements.next: Test rule-hidden positions, nested-dialog and pending-draft placement in both families and non-JVM runners; probe more modern prefixItems/items schema combinations beyond the focused duplicate-error adapter.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Components are quantities, not clock fields
requirements.statement: Duration picker components accept non-negative exact integers without clock-field caps; years, months, days, hours, minutes, seconds and separate weeks-only values retain their stored duration-string type.
requirements.next: The prior 31/23/59 sliders are replaced with exact integer fields and a weeks-only mode. Pure tests cover the exact-integer ceiling and all components; mounted Material/Cupertino JVM/iOS cases cover values above clock limits, immediate repeated edits with focus retained and an explicit switch to weeks mode. JS/Wasm compiles; browser/device interaction and invalid-import variants remain open.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Equivalent spellings are not the same data
requirements.statement: Existing equivalent duration spellings and leading zeros survive mount, opening and cancellation; canonical serialization happens only after an explicit picker edit.
requirements.next: Mounted tests retain P000W until an explicit edit, then write canonical P0D for an edited zero; a large component string survives Cancel. Direct-text drafts preserve imported spelling and reset on host replacement in JVM/iOS tests. Check caret/IME behavior and browser/device interaction.

requirements.statement: An explicit zero-duration edit serializes the canonical zero P0D, while Clear remains a separate operation and an untouched imported weeks-zero spelling remains unchanged.
requirements.next: Pure and paired mounted JVM/iOS tests distinguish untouched P000W from explicitly edited zero, which writes P0D. Check clear-on-array-position and browser/device interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Allow partial prefixes as local drafts
requirements.statement: Incomplete or invalid non-empty duration drafts do not overwrite the last committed value; staged picker edits Cancel or confirm only when valid.
requirements.next: Picker fields retain invalid local text, disable OK and report Pending without writing data; Cancel restores the committed value and Valid. Direct text uses native-family input compositions with a duration-aware local draft and pending owner. Mounted JVM/iOS tests cover partial P1, host replacement, valid correction and a picker edit replacing an invalid text draft. Repeated immediate component edits retain focus. Verify caret/IME, restrictions and browser/device interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Validate committed duration values through the JSON Schema validator
requirements.statement: Committed durations use schema format validation; uncommitted invalid drafts participate in pending validity without publishing additional errors, and UI format alone adds no schema constraint.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM/iOS cases show the schema validator rejects an imported committed bogus duration, direct correction restores Valid, and invalid uncommitted text reports Pending without replacing data. An invalid imported string under UI-only format remains schema-valid until edited; an invalid local draft then reports Pending and a valid correction restores Valid. Probe validator edge cases, target interaction and absence of additional-error publication.

requirements.statement: Duration picker changes stage in a dialog by default, Cancel discards, and OK on an untouched picker preserves the original string without a data write; showActions false commits valid component edits immediately.
requirements.next: Material uses AlertDialog and Cupertino uses CupertinoAlertDialog. Eighteen mounted JVM and iOS simulator cases cover open, untouched OK, edited OK, Cancel, invalid disabled OK, translated trigger, selected-mode no-op and immediate repeated edits. Cupertino numeric fields use CupertinoInputControl with Bulgarian invalid-number feedback; trigger and mode controls use CupertinoButton. JS/Wasm main compilation passes. Verify popup geometry, focus restoration and browser/device interaction.

requirements.statement: Password fields begin obscured and offer a localized, keyboard-operable reveal/hide action that changes presentation without writing data or changing validation.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM and iOS simulator tests verify English/Bulgarian action names, live locale and scoped override, zero data writes on reveal and read-only reveal access. Verify keyboard activation, visual masking, validation stability and browser/device interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Keep reveal and clear actions distinct
requirements.statement: Password reveal and clear actions are distinct; clearing obeys ordinary string clear semantics, and restriction, readonly and disabled mutation rules still apply.
requirements.next: Paired JVM and iOS simulator tests show separate reveal/clear names, no clear action in read-only mode, one clear write, maxLength prevention for restricted password edits, recovery from overlong imports and local restrict:false acceptance. Verify dynamic-property empty retention, disabled state, field errors and browser/device interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: A string password Control may request
requirements.statement: A password Control with variant otp and both minLength and maxLength renders maxLength character boxes; missing bounds fall back to the ordinary masked password field.
requirements.next: Twelve standalone OTP cases cover four boxes, missing-bound fallback, partial codes, keyboard insertion, narrow read-only layout and imported overflow recovery on JVM/iOS. Four further mounted cases pass on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm and verify native Material/Cupertino compact table cells keep an authored OTP variant as an ordinary masked field, with live Bulgarian feedback, reveal without writes and restricted repair. Verify standalone OTP browser/device runtime, large box counts and invalid bound combinations.

requirements.statement: OTP boxes preserve password masking, labels, readonly and string validation; keyboard navigation and paste retain leading zeros and commit partial strings.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM and iOS simulator tests verify partial minLength validation, leading-zero storage, arrow-key insertion, full replacement, reveal without a write, clear, read-only clear suppression, narrow action reachability and a visible imported overflow count that clears after recovery. Table cells retain ordinary masked password editing. Test actual clipboard paste, disabled behavior, screen reader semantics and device/browser interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The file control also selects arrays
requirements.statement: Homogeneous file-string arrays use the file Control; array-owned schema and mapped host errors display inline, with configured pre-touch filtering independent of stored validity.
requirements.next: JVM tests cover required, minItems, maxItems and host errors in both families; add item errors, blur interaction, real picker interaction and non-JVM execution.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The widget selects one local file
requirements.statement: A picker-backed scalar File Control selects one file and presents its stored filename with select and clear actions; it does not expose the encoded payload as an editable text field. Without a picker, a manual data or URL input remains available.
requirements.strength: project presentation contract inferred from spec and React/Svelte reference
requirements.next: Twelve paired Material/Cupertino mounted JVM cases cover filename replacement, clear, no raw editable payload, initial focus, required/help/error semantics, English/Bulgarian change, manual fallback, localized names for imported payload-only base64, and readonly/clearable action precedence. Verify browser/device interaction and direct screen-reader output.

requirements.statement: File-array count limits use minItems/maxItems under restrict; unrestricted edits can violate them; uniqueItems blocks duplicate encoded values and removal targets one index.
requirements.next: JVM tests cover boundary action state, unrestricted minItems/maxItems feedback, duplicate warning, ordered batch filtering with one commit, stale callback, and local restrict precedence; add platform picker interaction and occurrence-level duplicate size metadata.

requirements.statement: File-array clear-all writes an empty array, is disabled under restricted positive minItems, and individual removal and clear-all respect readonly and clearable with localized action text.
requirements.next: JVM tests cover restricted disablement, enabled clear-all mutation, clearable/readonly and local-option precedence, plus live translated clear-all label; add accessibility and target interaction.

requirements.statement: Rejected file operations give localized, themed local feedback without adding schema or host errors; feedback clears on success or external replacement.
requirements.next: JVM tests cover duplicate warning, live translation, external reset, rejected-size warning and read-failure error while retaining the old value. Built-in English/Bulgarian messages cover actions, warnings and singular/plural size errors with host override precedence. Add explicit validity/count assertions and target interaction.

requirements.statement: Base64 and byte file schemas store payload-only base64; binary stores a data URL with percent-encoded filename across platform pickers.
requirements.next: Shared encoding tests and all demo target compilations pass; run actual picker interactions on Android/JVM/JS/Wasm/iOS, review iOS MIME selection, and finish owned size-validation profile coverage.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Use the selected file's byte-size metadata
requirements.statement: File-size UI bounds use original byte metadata before reading; restricted violations preserve stored data and produce local warning, while accepted unrestricted violations contribute owned validation errors and pending reads affect command validity.
requirements.next: Mounted Material/Cupertino JVM tests prove scalar and array owned size errors, pending validity, host preservation, multi-file summary, removal, locale update, and cancellation/replacement/disposal races. All demo picker targets compile with metadata-first checks. Android, desktop and iOS share a post-read actual-byte check; focused tests prove missing-metadata fallback and unrestricted invalid storage. Add actual adapter failure/cancel interaction, real platform execution and size-validator profile coverage.

requirements.statement: Chooser cancellation clears the scoped form value, stays distinct from rejected selection, and stale asynchronous callbacks cannot restore the cleared value.
requirements.next: Paired JVM event tests cover scalar and array cancellation, late callback after cancellation, external replacement and disposal. Wasm/iOS demo adapters compile; run actual cancellation interactions on Android/JVM/JS/Wasm/iOS.

requirements.statement: Array file pickers select multiple files, retain accepted chooser order, apply per-file restrictions, and commit the accepted batch once; any read failure preserves previous attachments and a pending read cannot overwrite external data.
requirements.next: Paired JVM UI tests prove one commit, ordered accepted values, size/duplicate/count filtering, partial warning, external warning reset, read-failure preservation, and rejection of late batch/failure callbacks after external replacement with pending validity cleared; all demo targets compile. Run actual multi-selection and failure/cancel interactions on Android, desktop, iOS, JS and Wasm.

requirements.sourceAnchor: A file cell should use a compact
requirements.statement: File table cells use bounded filename presentation and accessible select, replace, remove and clear actions without repeated labels or descriptions; compact validation and operation feedback remains available through a severity icon with hover, focus and activation access.
requirements.next: Twenty-four mounted Material/Cupertino JVM table tests cover scalar replace/clear, ordered array batch, compact filename, validation icon, narrow-column clear reachability, live English/Bulgarian labels with host override, manual scalar/array editing and duplicate warning. Compact picker and manual-entry operation icons now sit beside Clear; action rows scroll to reveal the feedback in narrow cells, with paired geometry tests for read failure and duplicate warning. Encoding tests cover Unicode filenames. Add keyboard/hover tooltip interaction, native-target localization, no-picker accessibility/constraint checks and device/browser checks.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Select a Control whose schema is
requirements.statement: A type-null property selects a legible null Control that presents required state and mapped errors; a multi-type schema merely including null does not select it.
requirements.next: JVM tests cover pure-null selection, multi-type exclusion, required feedback and a nonmatching host error under opt-in filtering. Paired mounted tests now cover initial focus, strict description options, English/Bulgarian required semantics and error association. Verify direct screen-reader and non-JVM interaction.

requirements.statement: Null Control distinguishes missing from explicit JSON null in status and storage; clearing writes absence rather than null.
requirements.next: Material/Cupertino JVM tests cover set, clear and live English/Bulgarian built-in status without a host translator. Regional bg tags resolve to Bulgarian; unsupported de-DE falls back to English, and a distinct host translator overrides the built-in status. Verify schema replacement, host echo and target accessibility.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Register the control in the cells registry
requirements.statement: Null Control is registered in renderer and cell registries so a table cell uses its null presentation.
requirements.next: Mounted DispatchCell and actual portable array-table rows pass in both JVM families; compact null validation uses a focusable feedback icon and the checkbox's accessible error/name with no inline message. The real table test toggles missing to explicit null without changing the row. Verify target interaction and direct screen-reader behavior.

requirements.sourceAnchor: A renderer on a small screen SHOULD use platform-appropriate controls
requirements.statement: A renderer adapts presentation to constrained space while preserving the Control's semantic intent and stored value.
requirements.next: Mounted layout cases cover wrapping and auto-fit at narrow widths, and control-selection cases cover platform date presentation. Audit semantic equivalence, actual small-device geometry, keyboard/touch behavior, Android and browser runtime.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Explicit named breakpoint overrides are deferred
requirements.statement: Portable documents rely first on content- and container-driven layout; named breakpoint overrides are not part of the portable element language.
requirements.next: Material/Cupertino mounted layout tests cover wrap and minItemWidth resize behavior. Confirm renderer specification examples avoid undocumented breakpoint aliases and verify device/browser layout interactions. Host-selected alternate UI schemas remain outside the portable element language.

requirements.sourceAnchor: UI visibility is never an authorization boundary
requirements.statement: The service independently rejects unauthorized operations; hiding a Button or Control is presentation, not authorization enforcement.
requirements.next: The Kotlin renderer does not own service authorization. Document this boundary in host integration guidance and test an unauthorized service operation in an actual host before claiming this row.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Each renderer set SHOULD carry its own behaviour specification
requirements.statement: Each family documents canonical selection, option/schema effects, fallback, invalid values, accessibility, read-only/constraint behavior, internationalization and escape-hatch namespace.
requirements.next: Initial Material/Cupertino string and tuple entries and browser-only fallback boundaries are documented. Extend to all renderer/cell entries with exact option types, schema effects, target evidence and usability behavior.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Every entry MUST state its provenance
requirements.statement: Every renderer behavior entry states provenance and exact selection, options/defaults/precedence, schema keyword effects, invalid/permission fallback and family/version applicability.
requirements.next: The new catalog records provenance and behavior for text and tuple entries; registry inventory lists all Material/Cupertino/extended entries but is not a behavior specification. Add per-option origin exceptions and remaining entries before closure.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Entries MUST include a concrete schema and UI-schema selection example
requirements.statement: Each renderer behavior entry includes a selecting schema/UI-schema example and a misleading incompatible-schema example.
requirements.next: The initial string and tuple entries include both selecting and incompatible examples. Add equivalent examples for every remaining renderer and cell profile.

requirements.sourceAnchor: A feature present in one family MUST NOT be described as supported by all
requirements.statement: Capability claims distinguish Material, Cupertino and optional extended provenance and applicability rather than treating package membership as family support.
requirements.next: Initial entries separate Material/Cupertino compositions and mark AG Grid, Monaco and TemplateLayout as unsupported browser profiles. Audit delegated Cupertino entries and every optional extended profile before making family-wide claims.

requirements.sourceAnchor: views never changes the save format
requirements.statement: Temporal options.views controls picker presentation independently of dateSaveFormat, timeSaveFormat or dateTimeSaveFormat; view granularity must never change serialized storage.
requirements.applicability: portable temporal storage with platform picker presentation
requirements.next: Six mounted views-plus-save-format typed-edit cases pass on JVM and iOS simulator. Fourteen mounted time-column and sixteen mounted date-view cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser across both families, including date/time half fallback, hidden components, bounds and Bulgarian labels. Native pickers without authored views preserve seconds. A date-time edit crossing a daylight-saving transition can shift the stored UTC hour; settle timezone policy and verify Android interaction and native calendar landing before full conformance.

requirements.sourceAnchor: An array naming no view of a kind the control uses
requirements.statement: A temporal views array with no applicable date or time view leaves that half to the display format; unusable views are ignored without blanking the picker.
requirements.next: Authored time views filter visible columns and the finest date view selects day, month or year mode in Material/Cupertino date and date-time controls. Arrays with no applicable view for one half fall back to that half of the display format. Six pure and 30 mounted cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser across both families. Verify Android interaction, native day-calendar landing and timezone behavior before certifying the clause.

requirements.statement: options.focus requests initial focus once when the primary input mounts visible and focusable; data, locale and option rerenders do not reclaim it. Several requests have no portable guaranteed winner.
requirements.next: Text input and enum/oneOf radio focus has an 18-case Material/Cupertino mounted class passing on JVM and iOS simulator; 16 cases passed in JS before two string-option cases were added. Checkbox, switch and slider have twelve mounted JVM cases, including the single-value button, disabled-then-enabled behavior and strict Boolean parsing. Six mounted JVM cases cover enum, oneOf and searchable choice anchors in both families. Fourteen array-choice mounted JVM cases now cover checkbox arrays, multi-select and finite/free chips: the first eligible checkbox or primary add/token input receives focus once, menus stay closed, local false and quoted true suppress a global request, disabled-then-enabled add does not request late focus, and data/locale/option rerenders do not reclaim focus or write data. Full affected JVM suites pass 18 Compose, 77 Material, six Cupertino and 1,647 examples-compose tests; JS, Wasm and iOS test sources compile. Other controls, hidden remounts, Android and non-JVM interaction remain open.

requirements.statement: hideRequiredAsterisk hides only the visual marker; required validation and accessible required-state information remain, with the effective Boolean option resolved locally before global configuration.
requirements.next: Two mounted Material/Cupertino text-input cases pass on JVM and iOS simulator. Twelve Boolean/slider, eight radio/select and eight array-choice mounted JVM cases cover both families, live English/Bulgarian required state, hidden/visible markers, local false over global true and quoted-Boolean rejection. Checkbox arrays, multi-select and finite/free chips now retain required semantics on their interactive controls. Full affected JVM suites pass 18 Compose, 77 Material, six Cupertino and 1,625 examples-compose tests; JS, Wasm and iOS test sources compile. Audit remaining controls, accessible help/error associations, Android, native assistive technology and browser interaction.

requirements.statement: showUnfocusedDescription controls whether applicable help is visible without focus; validation errors remain visible and may appear with help, and visible help and errors should be associated accessibly with the input.
requirements.next: Paired mounted Material/Cupertino text-input cases pass on JVM and iOS simulator. Eight array-choice, two radio, six enum/oneOf selector, six Boolean/slider, six mixed anyOf text/enum, four portable array-table, four ListWithDetail, six picker-only color and eight noncompact file-array mounted JVM cases cover both families. These apply strict Boolean showUnfocusedDescription, show help beside validation errors, reveal help on focus, hide it after focus moves away, and associate visible feedback with interactive semantics. The mixed anyOf control retains editable suggestions under Cupertino's specific tester; portable table/ListWithDetail use Add, picker-only color uses Choose color, and file arrays use Choose file or their manual field as primary focus/feedback targets. Color help follows picker controls so pointer focus does not move the clicked target. Live English/Bulgarian changes update required state without mount writes. Checkbox-array help hide on blur is deferred through the pointer gesture so an imported popup stays open. Full affected JVM suites pass 383 extended and 1,681 examples-compose tests; JS, Wasm and iOS test sources compile. Compact file cells, other controls and direct screen-reader, Android and browser interaction remain open.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Use the existing translator for all temporal draft feedback
requirements.statement: Temporal draft feedback uses the translator, formats bounds for active locale/display format, associates feedback accessibly, updates with state/locale and clears after correction or discard.
requirements.next: English/Bulgarian range text, display-format bounds, picker feedback and editor/confirmation error semantics pass focused temporal tests on JVM and iOS simulator. Eight imported Material/Cupertino range cases pass on JVM, iOS, JS browser and Wasm browser: typed edits at inclusive/exclusive date, time and date-time bounds show feedback and clear it after repair. Four imported picker cases verify unrestricted out-of-range commit with persistent validation and exclusive-minimum rejection followed by valid selection on all four targets. Malformed $data references have localized restricted-picker feedback. Verify other imported picker bounds, screen readers, pending-draft semantics and schema compilation diagnostics.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Incomplete edits should remain local while being
requirements.statement: Incomplete temporal edits remain local and do not overwrite committed data; unresolved drafts participate in pending-edit validity.
requirements.next: JVM tests cover six family/format partial edits, corrected publication, host replacement, four schema/UI contract changes and owner disposal. Test config changes, focus, submission gating, accessibility, rapid edits and non-JVM interaction.

requirements.statement: Completed typed and picker edits use the same save-format contract and remain subject to schema validation.
requirements.next: Configured save formats and UTC-normalized offset-bearing Time imports pass JVM tests in both families. Shared schema/picker bound ordering covers offsets and fractional seconds. Square-bracket literal format text round-trips through formatting, masking and parsing on JVM/iOS simulator/JS browser/Wasm browser. The imported temporal-controls fixture now verifies schema-selected date display without a mount write and an authored YYYY.MM month edit saved as YYYY-MM in both families on JVM/iOS simulator. The default date-time policy retains local wall time on date edits and can shift the stored UTC hour across DST. Verify the fixture's other controls, custom offset-token formats, DST transitions and Android interaction.

requirements.statement: Temporal showActions defaults false: false commits valid picker selections immediately, while true stages them until OK and lets Cancel discard the draft; typed input commits independently.
requirements.next: All three temporal control formats now default showActions false in Material and Cupertino. Standalone date/time and date-time coarse views commit valid choices immediately; Cupertino's combined native wheel commits immediately, and Material's native date step commits before Next. The immediate date step retains Next for navigation but omits Cancel; explicit true staging remains tested. Material date-time uses portable time columns for the display-format fallback. The apparent 10-to-15 hour mismatch was local hour 10 serialized as 15:00Z under the documented local-wall-time policy. The 34 focused mounted cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser; Material's native date dialog now sets its displayed month to the stored date, with a JVM mounted regression. The pinned Material3 JS day-cell accessibility description can be one day behind its UTC selection in a western browser timezone; JS day-cell accessibility and Android interaction remain open.

requirements.statement: Time and date-time pickers use 24-hour interaction by default; ampm true requests 12-hour interaction without changing display or save formats.
requirements.next: Material and Cupertino time and date-time controls interpret absent and false ampm as 24-hour interaction, and true as 12-hour interaction. Focused mounted cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser. Verify Android and device accessibility before full conformance.

requirements.statement: Runtime author diagnostics carry stable machine-readable codes, severity, message and optional details.
requirements.next: Layout diagnostics use stable codes and both-family callbacks on JVM; unify other renderer diagnostics and verify target delivery.

requirements.statement: Misconfiguration diagnostics go to the form author rather than becoming field errors for the form user.
requirements.next: Both-family JVM layout callback tests pass without inline diagnostic text; verify other codes, host lifecycle and target execution.

requirements.statement: A failure leaving visible content missing also provides an accessible in-place explanation.
requirements.next: Unresolved property scopes, unsupported UI types and unavailable cell renderers show text-semantic fallbacks in English or Bulgarian in mounted shared dispatch. Audit other missing-content failures, real table-cell entry and direct screen-reader behavior.

requirements.statement: Every declared diagnostic code has an emitting condition and a test proving delivery.
requirements.next: Mounted unsupported elements and shared cell dispatch emit renderer.unavailable and cell.unavailable once each, retaining stable codes across locale changes. A Button with no host handler emits action.unhandled on press, including after late reporter installation. Inventory remaining declared codes and test real table-cell entry.

requirements.statement: Text interpolation treats single braces as expressions and double opening/closing braces as literal braces, independently of the experimental overlay profile.
requirements.next: Pure JVM, iOS simulator and Wasm browser tests plus 28 mounted Material/Cupertino Label cases on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm cover single and literal braces. Verify the remaining CEL grammar and physical-device interaction.

requirements.statement: A double-braced dynamic path remains literal text and warns that it may be an unintended Mustache-style expression.
requirements.next: Pure JVM/iOS/Wasm and mounted Material/Cupertino JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm cases keep a double-braced dynamic path literal and report a warning. Verify translated warning text, less common escaped path spellings and physical-device interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The canonical expression profile is CEL.
requirements.statement: Label message interpolation uses CEL expression semantics, including Unicode code-point string size and ordering; ICU message patterns remain a separate extension.
requirements.next: The strict portable subset matches CEL string size and ordering in pure and mounted Material/Cupertino cases on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm. It evaluates bounded all, exists, exists_one, map and filter over JSON lists/maps, including a 5,000-item reference case, with lexical variables and a depth/work limit; mounted both-family cases update after host data replacement. Map/filter support list elements or map keys, chained calls and three-argument filtered map. CEL list and string-key JSON map literals compose with membership, size and macros; missing or invalid entries and duplicate keys diagnose. A mounted map-literal equality case updates after host data replacement. CEL all/exists defer predicate errors until a decisive false/true can override them, whereas exists_one reports any predicate error; map/filter per-element errors and limit failures remain immediate. Logical AND/OR also absorb ordinary operand errors when the other operand is decisive, while evaluation-limit failures remain immediate. Postfix indexing now selects from list/map literals and map/filter results, including nested indexes and live host-data updates. The focused 45 pure and 32 mounted Label cases pass on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm; the full extended-renderers JVM suite passes 375 tests and Android main compiles. CEL r/R raw string literals preserve backslashes in quoted text and map keys. string() converts string, Boolean and signed integer JSON scalars; dyn() preserves runtime values without a type checker. Triple-quoted strings, including raw multiline forms, now work across template and expression scanners; bytes literals, remaining extreme string(double) edge-case parity and full CEL type checking remain open. The minimum positive and negative subnormal now use the reference shortest decimal on all four targets; the minimum normal, maximum finite and binary64 integer precision boundaries also pass. Finite string(double) now uses locale-independent fixed/scientific formatting and preserves signed zero across targets, with a live mounted update. Receiver-style size() works on strings/lists/maps, and contains(), startsWith() and endsWith() work on strings, including literal and filtered receivers with live host-data updates. List concatenation with + composes with size, indexing and macros under a 10,000-element output cap. Portable bool, int and double JSON-scalar conversions now handle valid strings, truncation and range errors; uint, bytes, type values, extreme string(double) parity and RE2 matches() remain open. The optional React/Svelte translate(key, fallback) overload passes the authored fallback to the host translator without displacing a catalog hit. Only English and Bulgarian locale bundles are shipped. Finish non-string CEL map keys, remaining grammar/type checking, runtime parity and ICU separation audit.

requirements.statement: An expression authoring error such as an unknown root/function or type mismatch is reported without throwing out of the Label.
requirements.next: The imported five-author-error category keeps label text and reports visible diagnostics in both families on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm; pure tests also cover wrong key types. Audit remaining CEL author errors and physical-device diagnostic presentation.

requirements.statement: Absent data below a resolved namespace, including missing nested properties and out-of-range list indexes, renders as empty text without an author diagnostic.
requirements.next: Large signed list indexes pass pure JVM/iOS/Wasm tests and live selected-row replacement in both families on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm. Verify additional nested absence and physical-device presentation.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The canonical expression profile is CEL.
requirements.statement: The CEL has macro checks field presence through select syntax, including a key with a null value, and rejects non-field expressions.
requirements.next: Pure JVM/iOS/Wasm and paired mounted JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm tests cover null versus missing, nested map selection and invalid macro forms; audit complete CEL macro grammar and physical-device interaction.

requirements.statement: Translated text may access only declared textParams and locale; a direct data path in translated text reports an authoring error.
requirements.next: An injected translation that introduces {data.name} reports an author error after a live locale switch in both JVM families while declared {person} still reads data; verify browser/native target UI and real catalog fallback.

requirements.statement: Expressions cannot assign, execute statements or call unregistered host functions; lookup reads only owned JSON values.
requirements.next: The strict evaluator and JSON-safe scopes cover selected attempts; add an adversarial syntax corpus and target execution.

requirements.statement: Locale-aware number, currency and date formatting are reachable from expressions.
requirements.next: Registered functions and imported Label UI pass on JVM; verify all locale variants and target runtime behavior.

requirements.statement: Authors call formatting functions explicitly; scalar substitution does not silently apply locale number/date formatting.
requirements.next: Pure and imported Label cases distinguish raw year/amount from formatted values; verify all host locales and targets.

requirements.statement: A date-only calendar value is formatted in UTC so viewer time zones do not shift its date.
requirements.next: Pure JVM and time-zone tests exist; verify iOS/JS/Wasm formatting and boundary time zones.

requirements.statement: Substituted values are escaped before Markdown parsing so their markup syntax cannot create links or other formatting.
requirements.next: Pure hostile-link case and mounted markup checks exist on JVM; verify all Markdown constructs and browser output.

requirements.statement: Escaping applies only to substituted values; authored surrounding Markdown remains active.
requirements.next: Pure bold-literal/substitution tests pass; verify translated markup and target UI.

requirements.statement: Interpolation failures do not throw from the renderer; object/list values without text form report an authoring error instead of stringifying.
requirements.next: Focused pure and mounted JVM diagnostics exist; audit all expression and template failure paths.

requirements.statement: Only implementation-registered functions are callable from expressions.
requirements.next: Unknown-function and registered formatting/translation cases pass; probe callable host values and target execution.

requirements.statement: Functions supplied in context or data are neither callable nor exposed as readable expression values.
requirements.next: JSON-safe config/context and unknown-function tests cover selected cases; audit every host-context conversion and target.

requirements.statement: A JSON key named constructor or another host-language name reads normally and does not hide sibling keys.
requirements.next: Pure JVM constructor/toString and sibling cases pass; execute on JS/iOS/Wasm and mounted forms.

requirements.statement: Renderer-owned strings use stable namespace keys rather than their English wording.
requirements.next: Extended presentation strings and shared Material/Cupertino control, mixed, group, accordion and tuple chrome now use stable bundle keys; inventory remaining strings.

requirements.statement: A renderer set keeps its complete default string set in an enumerable catalog.
requirements.next: The color picker now enumerates English/Bulgarian static and generated keys with matching key sets; inventory remaining renderer strings and establish complete per-family catalogs.

requirements.statement: Portable catalog lookup prefers an exact own dotted key, then traverses nested own properties and accepts only a string final value.
requirements.next: Exact dotted and nested string lookup passes pure core tests; imported nested fixture catalogs flatten with literal dotted precedence and render in both families on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm. Extend to all portable catalog consumers and adversarial keys.

requirements.statement: Every renderer-owned translation lookup supplies a documented default message.
requirements.next: The shared helper plus File, Link, ImageView, profile and native-control tests pass documented locale defaults to translators; audit remaining calls.

requirements.statement: Form catalog overrides renderer locale bundle, which becomes the translator default; a documented default is last.
requirements.next: Native controls, password/temporal pickers and mixed/group/tuple chrome pass selected bundle precedence tests; tuple defaults and host overrides pass on JVM/iOS simulator. Extend checks to remaining renderer strings.

requirements.statement: A regional locale falls back to its base language bundle before the documented default.
requirements.next: Regional fallback passes core/extended/material target tests plus mounted native-control, mixed/group/tuple, password, temporal and Link/ImageView JVM cases; tuple locale cases also pass on iOS simulator. Cover remaining bundles and target UI.

requirements.statement: Strings visible on initial mount resolve synchronously to the active locale.
requirements.next: Native controls, mixed/group chrome, extended profiles, Link/ImageView failures and AG Grid fallback show locale defaults on initial JVM mount. Shared tuple complex-position summaries, edit action and dialog controls now use English/Bulgarian defaults without a host translator; paired Material/Cupertino mounted tests cover initial Bulgarian count text and a live host override on JVM, JS browser, Wasm browser and iOS simulator. The 97-case tuple UI class passes on each target, and Android main compiles. Cover remaining renderers, accessibility and Android runtime.

requirements.statement: The basic Markdown profile renders paragraphs, line breaks, emphasis, inline code, links, and ordered and unordered lists.
requirements.next: Kotlin now renders ordered, unordered and nested items as Compose collections with item semantics in paired JVM tests; verify native/browser accessibility and list layout.

requirements.next: JVM/iOS simulator/JS browser/Wasm browser pure excluded-grammar cases pass; expand adversarial parser cases and browser semantics.

Mounted JVM tests cover heading and table-header semantics; pure tests check custom-scheme/refused links in nested blocks. Verify native/browser UI behavior and further adversarial grammar cases.

requirements.statement: Markdown output is sanitized after parsing, or built directly from an allowlisted token tree without producing unsanitized markup.
