requirements.statement: A parser scheme allowlist cannot narrow the configured URL policy before target checking.
requirements.next: Custom scheme is accepted under the host policy and refused target counts are reported on JVM; verify browser click behavior.

requirements.statement: Unknown markup requests and Markdown disabled by the host report a diagnostic while retaining authored text.
requirements.next: Paired mounted Material/Cupertino JVM cases cover unknown and disabled requests; verify all targets.

requirements.statement: Markdown may default to enabled.
requirements.next: Default-enabled path has pure and mounted JVM evidence; document host opt-out and verify target UI.

requirements.statement: Typography resolves from element option, then host markup typography setting, then true.
requirements.next: Pure precedence and paired mounted JVM cases pass; Material typography has a measurable size difference while Cupertino uses native CupertinoText. Verify visual theme behavior on native/browser targets.

requirements.statement: Typography can be switched off without disabling Markdown parsing.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM cases retain bold spans and policy-checked links under both wrapper settings.

requirements.statement: A host-library text component receives block versus inline content in a structurally valid way.
requirements.next: Material Text and CupertinoText receive the full AnnotatedString without nested paragraph markup; verify browser semantics and target accessibility.

requirements.statement: disableAdd and disableRemove default false, resolve element options over top-level config, suppress insertion or deletion without suppressing reorder or existing-value editing, and cannot override readonly or restricted counts.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM tests cover collection, checkbox, chips, multi-select and file arrays in both families; verify target UI behavior and remaining array operation entry points.

requirements.statement: Array action handlers guard current permission, and a pending delete confirmation or asynchronous add cannot grant permission after flags change.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM cases revoke deletion during confirmation and file addition during picker operation. Audit keyboard, context-menu, duplication, paste and batch entry points where supported.

requirements.statement: Unknown host Markdown profile values safely fall back to basic without an author diagnostic.
requirements.next: Pure profile resolution and paired mounted JVM cases verify that unknown values retain literal heading/table syntax without a diagnostic. Verify target UI behavior.

requirements.statement: The validator supports applicable data-dependent keyword values and reports its unsupported Ajv profile capabilities explicitly.
requirements.next: The four temporal format comparison keywords validate literal and resolvable $data bounds, including hidden fields, on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm core tests and JVM/iOS mounted tests. Portable comparators include Ajv's iso-time and iso-date-time ordering alongside date/time/date-time, including lexically ordered malformed date and ISO bound strings; ISO formats have portable format assertions but no picker renderer. Invalid pointer syntax, direct-path relative depth, missing format, formats without a registered comparator and non-string literal bounds yield compile-time keyword-path errors even with absent data. Reusable definitions defer relative-depth checking to the applied instance path. General $data keywords, indirect-path depth, custom comparator registration and dynamic-schema recompilation cost remain open.

requirements.statement: Property dependencies do not infer control creation or visibility; missing dependent-property errors reach the affected control when rendered, and clearing the trigger preserves independent dependent data.
requirements.next: Dependency presence/whole-object behavior and indexed fallback pass core tests on JVM, iOS, JS and Wasm. The validator adapter now expands grouped dependencies, dependentRequired and schema-valued required errors into one routed error per absent property, including names with punctuation. All 20 Material/Cupertino mounted dependency tests pass on JVM and iOS; the earlier 18 pass on JS and Wasm browsers. The two new multi-dependent UI cases compile for JS/Wasm, but JS browser execution stalled and the Wasm Compose executable exceeded local disk space. Android interaction and broader dependency configurations remain open.

requirements.statement: Shared detail selection prefers inline UI schema, then case-insensitive GENERATE without registry lookup, then the highest ranked registered schema, then generated fallback.
requirements.next: Core precedence and Material/Cupertino object, array, and list-with-detail mode switching pass JVM and iOS simulator mounted tests. Broader registry ranking, tie, and other renderer integrations remain to audit.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Rendering a generated form MUST NOT
requirements.statement: Generated detail forms dispatch nested elements normally and do not initialize or overwrite missing data during render.
requirements.next: Material/Cupertino object detail with a missing object stays absent on mount and creates it only after a text edit on JVM and iOS simulator. Array/list missing-data cases and other targets remain to verify.

requirements.statement: Object detail rendering guards against re-entering the same selected UI schema at the same data path.
requirements.next: Existing mounted Material/Cupertino self-matching registry cases show a generated fallback and one diagnostic without data writes on JVM; iOS, nested distinct-path recursion, and wider renderer coverage remain to verify.

requirements.statement: UI-schema registry testers are synchronous, side-effect-free selectors returning NOT_APPLICABLE or a nonnegative rank; highest rank wins and first registration wins ties.
requirements.next: The typed Kotlin tester API is synchronous and returns Int ranks; focused JVM and iOS tests cover NOT_APPLICABLE, zero rank, highest rank, tie order and schema-path/item-path context. Side-effect freedom and invocation-count independence remain caller obligations and are not runtime-enforced.

requirements.statement: Detail scopes resolve relative to the selected object or item schema while preserving its data path and root schema references; UI-schema and renderer registries remain distinct selection steps.
requirements.next: Expanded second-row registered details use the rows.1 tester path; their relative name control edits only rows.1, including an item $ref into root $defs. All four mounted cases pass on JVM and iOS simulator. Nested object references, list/tuple variants, and other targets remain to verify.

requirements.statement: Explicit Add initializes a new value from the item schema, deep-copying explicit JSON container defaults and preserving falsy defaults; object properties receive only declared defaults, not type placeholders.
requirements.next: Core JVM/iOS tests cover nested explicit default copy, false/zero/null, primitive fallbacks and declared-only object properties. Four Material/Cupertino table/expandable mounted cases on JVM/iOS preserve an existing item and append two object defaults. Temporal schema-format initialization, constraints and combinator cases need more targeted evidence.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Rendering an existing item MUST NOT
requirements.statement: Rendering existing array items does not repeat initialization or overwrite data; explicit object/array defaults for successive additions have independent containers and leave the schema unchanged.
requirements.next: Focused JVM/iOS core identity checks show new nested JSON containers on each call, distinct from schema defaults; mounted Material/Cupertino table/expandable tests show zero writes on mount and preserve an existing row through two Adds. JSON values are immutable; wider render modes, branch validity and browser/Android interaction remain open.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Provide accessible feedback for object-level errors
requirements.statement: Object-level errors remain visible and accessible beside an object editor even when its generated or registered detail layout has no matching input.
requirements.next: Exact-path and unrepresented descendant errors receive Error semantics beside the Material/Cupertino object detail. Six mounted cases pass on JVM/iOS with a label-only detail, a bound field and a rule-hidden field; the hidden field becomes visible without duplicate summary feedback when host data changes. Schema-generated object errors, deep nested layouts, screen readers, browser/Android interaction and all validation modes remain to verify.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Hiding a control does not discard its errors
requirements.statement: A rule-hidden detail control remains subject to validation, and its eligible errors stay discoverable without making the control visible.
requirements.next: The object editor excludes rule-hidden detail bindings from represented error scopes. Paired Material/Cupertino mounted cases show accessible hidden-field feedback and one message after the field becomes visible, without data writes, on JVM and iOS simulator. Nested rule paths, hidden layout containers, display-mode filtering and screen-reader behavior remain open.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Errors at the array's own path
requirements.statement: Array-level errors come from structured exact-path selection, remain separate from descendant summaries and stay accessible near an empty array even when child summaries are hidden.
requirements.next: Six new empty-array Material/Cupertino expandable, table and list cases verify minItems text with Error semantics while child summary is hidden, on JVM/iOS. Six existing cases verify own-array text survives indicator and summary options. Cupertino delegates these shared paths. Wider array modes, other targets and screen readers remain open.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Item badges and summaries associate errors by path segment
requirements.statement: Array item badges associate normalized schema and host errors by complete path segment, and count markers have an explanatory accessible name.
requirements.next: Core grouping separates rows.1 from rows.10, keeps array-own errors out of descendants and handles escaped required/host paths; mounted Material/Cupertino item badges carry translated content descriptions and row-detail navigation identifies the failing item on JVM/iOS. Reorder/deletion remapping, all collection modes and screen-reader behavior remain open.

requirements.statement: The validator applies contains and supported minContains/maxContains to matching entries across the full array, keeps tuple position validation separate, and exposes empty-array violations at the array path.
requirements.next: Four focused core cases pass on JVM/iOS for default one match, min/max match counts, inert count keywords without contains and tuple prefix/tail separation. Six Material/Cupertino mounted empty-array cases pass on JVM/iOS with accessible own-array contains feedback and live host repair. Draft-07 count-keyword behavior, reference-rich matching, JS/Wasm validation and other targets remain open.

requirements.statement: Restricted discrete deletion should preserve a currently satisfied contains minimum when matching can be evaluated reliably, using current validator dialect without changing data.
requirements.next: The shared compiled-validator guard is wired into expandable, table, list-with-detail and Material/Cupertino tuple tail Delete state, requests, confirmations and commits under restrict. Three original core helper, 18 mounted standard-array and all 89 tuple cases pass on JVM/iOS. Six standard-array and two tuple host-replacement cases show pending confirmation closes and newly matching Delete becomes disabled without a data write. Enum checkboxes, multi-select and chips apply the same guard to restricted removals, including out-of-choice values; 54 focused mounted cases pass on JVM across the checkbox and multi-select suites. File-array Remove and Clear all now guard satisfied contains minima, with a fourth core helper and 68 mounted file-array cases passing on JVM. Remaining: other mutation paths and targets, explicit validation-cost measurement and custom validator behavior.

requirements.statement: Object and array table cells show a decorative type marker only when showTypeIndicator resolves true, with cell options overriding collection options and the top-level config; explicit false wins, scalar cells have no marker, and summary text is unchanged.
requirements.next: Five core and ten mounted Material/Cupertino composite-cell cases pass on JVM/iOS; new cases verify default absence, global true, local false, object/array-only markers and absence from text semantics. Core/Material JS and Wasm compilation passes. AG Grid hosting, browser/device interaction, theme contrast and broader option placement remain open.

requirements.statement: Composite-cell detail dialogs apply explicit or localized action labels, resolve optional Clear/Remove from cell, collection and global options, keep those actions private until Apply, cancel superseded drafts and honor clearable and structural restrict rules.
requirements.next: Four core option/structural cases pass on JVM and the earlier three plus four bundle cases pass on iOS. Twenty mounted composite-cell and eight row-detail cases pass on JVM/iOS after modal action guards; the shared Material renderer compiles on JS/Wasm. Background scalar cells and table Add/Delete/Move/Edit, external clear, panel selection and pagination are disabled while a cell or row dialog is open, then restored on Cancel. Draft fields and dialog actions stay active. The full mounted JVM suite passed 1020 tests before the later live-option, modal and tooltip changes. Clear/Remove are draft-only, stale child callbacks are revision-guarded, a nonempty removal uses confirmation, parent-required removal remains available, protected children block Empty and clearable false hides both. Localized Apply/Cancel tooltip wrappers are present in both families, but desktop hover testing did not expose them from the separate dialog popup. Composite array-cell Empty now uses the active validator to block an empty draft that violates object/boolean contains or composed structural minima under restrict; minContains zero remains clearable. Focused core cases cover the composed object/array constraints and a plain-composite no-validation fast path; paired mounted Material/Cupertino contains cases pass on JVM. Physical hover/focus, other wider restrict constraints, nested-dialog pending work and browser interaction remain open.

requirements.sourceAnchor: the message MUST also be on the accessible name
requirements.statement: A compact table cell error marker includes its localized validation message in the accessible name when the inline message is suppressed.
requirements.next: The shared table frame appends the localized error message to the cell marker's accessible name while retaining hover tooltip and state description; compact native Material/Cupertino Boolean cells use that marker. Registered custom cells retain it by default; cells that own their feedback opt out. Four paired mounted registered-cell cases pass on JVM and JS browser, including a host error in the accessible name, header suppression, host repair and no form write. Compact file picker and manual-entry cells put the translated error on the interactive control's accessible name and error semantics. Compact Material/Cupertino text inputs now likewise suppress inline imported-value text while exposing a hover tooltip, accessible name and error semantics; paired base text/numeric/password/temporal cells and six extended formatted-cell conflict cases pass on JVM. The full 2,080-case demo JVM suite passes after Boolean-cell and collection-summary tests were corrected to expect Bulgarian accessible names following a locale switch. Forty-four earlier focused mounted cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser, including Bulgarian text and clearing after correction. Verify direct screen-reader output, Android interaction and broader native Cupertino cell parity.

requirements.sourceAnchor: when composition describes one unambiguous scalar editor
requirements.statement: A scalar with validation-only combinator branches renders one editor at the outer Control path and retains full composed-schema validation.
requirements.next: Imported attendee anyOf and seats-per-table oneOf render one editable number each in Material/Cupertino JVM and iOS simulator tests. Their invalid edits show field errors that clear after correction. The Draft-07 metaschema's definition-backed minLength allOf renders one labelled integer editor in paired JVM/iOS simulator tests; a four-case JS browser run also passed once with observed XML before later stalled runs cleared it. Safe allOf numeric bounds prevent a new negative value under default restrict while preserving repair of an imported invalid value; explicit restrict false stores -1 and shows the full-schema minimum error. Const choices and conflicting types retain separate presentations. Verify other reference shapes, outer presentation options, reliable browser rerun/combinator cases, Android interaction and native input attributes.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The enclosing properties followed by all branch forms in schema order
requirements.statement: AllOfRenderer renders enclosing properties before every branch form at the same data path, without a branch selector; a matching registered UI schema may provide a combined form.
requirements.next: Imported equipment shows its enclosing Projector name, then asset tag and working state with no mount write in Material/Cupertino JVM and iOS simulator UI tests. Verify explicit registered combined UI schemas, duplicate property constraints, branch editing, validation visibility and mounted browser/Android interaction.

requirements.statement: ListWithDetail navigation has a bounded scroll height only when needed, while short lists retain natural height and the selected detail remains independent.
requirements.next: Material ListWithDetail and Cupertino's currently delegated renderer let a short list keep natural height and cap a 30-item list at 384 dp. Mounted touch and Page Down cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser; wheel cases pass on JVM, JS browser and Wasm browser. Each input changes the navigation scroll offset while the selected detail editor stays in place and data is unchanged. Paired mounted nested row-detail dialog cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser, confirming the 384 dp cap, list scrolling, stationary selected editor and unchanged data. Android interaction, direct accessibility output and native Cupertino presentation remain to verify.

requirements.statement: Text entry preserves composition-based input; string length restrictions count the stored representation rather than UTF-16 code units or display-only text.
requirements.next: Stored string length uses Unicode code points in the shared restricted edit helper. Composition-based IME interaction remains unverified on Android, iOS and desktop; verify it before claiming this clause.

requirements.sourceAnchor: An action that consumes form data MUST resolve pending edits
requirements.statement: Actions consuming form data resolve pending edits before reading the current data and validation; an unresolved draft does not silently dispatch an older snapshot, and Clear supersedes queued edits.
requirements.next: Material/Cupertino mounted Button tests prove that an unresolved date draft blocks dispatch with Bulgarian feedback and a corrected edit reaches the handler with current data on JVM/iOS. Material searchable enum/oneOf queries now report Pending until explicit selection or dismissal; focused mounted JVM/iOS cases pass. The Button guards at click and coroutine start. A generic flush mechanism for committable debounced edits, keyboard activation and other data-consuming actions remain open.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The path alone is insufficient evidence
requirements.statement: Queued editors distinguish normal host echo of their own commit from an external value replacing the same path, and cancel obsolete writes after index shifts or target changes.
requirements.next: Numeric draft, composite-cell session and Material searchable choice tests cover selected host replacements: a choice host update discards its pending search and menu without a data write. Audit every editor with queued work and path-stable array-index shifts; direct delayed-write host-echo evidence is missing.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The selected value MUST retain its JSON type
requirements.statement: Finite choices preserve the selected value's JSON type and distinguish numeric 1 from string 1 independently of labels or widget identity; unsupported shapes and unknown existing values require a documented nonmutating fallback.
requirements.next: Fifty-six mounted typed-choice cases pass on JVM/iOS: Material/Cupertino plain-enum and const-oneOf radios and dropdowns retain typed scalar, null, object and array values. Equal-label options remain separate menu/radio entries with accessible names that include the JSON value, committing number 1 versus string 1 correctly. Four live locale cases prove translated Bulgarian label collisions retain selection and stored identity. Radio groups honor nested radio vertical defaults, local false, horizontal wrapping and vertical stacking with localized group semantics; six further keyboard cases cover directional/RTL navigation and activation. Explicit enum lists win over generic Boolean selection while Boolean const agreement controls retain their prior precedence. Empty options show English/Bulgarian text through a stable host key. Shared radio Clear removes a selected null property, respects live clearable/readonly/disabled changes and current property paths, and disappears after removal. Dropdowns and radios display unknown number 42 without mount writes; radio groups distinguish missing from explicit null and show a localized current-value warning. Audit array choices, physical screen-reader output and browser/device interaction.

requirements.statement: Radio groups support directional keyboard navigation consistent with orientation and RTL, Space activation, label activation, selected-radio stability and the shared Clear action for present values.
requirements.next: Eight mounted JVM/iOS cases cover horizontal Right, vertical Down, RTL Left, Space activation, clickable labels, selected-radio stability and Enter-activated Clear in Material/Cupertino. Ten further mounted JVM/iOS cases cover shared Clear for selected null, English/Bulgarian text, required validity, live clearable/readonly/disabled guards and current property paths. Four JVM image cases verify Clear hide, pointer hover/exit and keyboard focus. Verify physical input on devices and browser accessibility.

requirements.sourceAnchor: A renderer MUST NOT silently replace existing form data
requirements.statement: Out-of-domain existing values remain in form data and visible for repair until an explicit edit; filtering finite choices does not substitute or clear them.
requirements.next: Material/Cupertino dropdowns and radios display imported number 42 and preserve it until explicit selection. Plain-enum and const-oneOf standard/searchable dropdowns show explicit out-of-domain null as null under an English/Bulgarian warning; missing data stays blank. Multi-select/chips expose imported null and object shapes, and radio groups show the actual JSON value. The automatic enum-array checkbox renderer shows unknown occurrences and non-array values without a mount write; non-array status now also reaches each checkbox's accessible feedback. Unknown occurrences have guarded, positional removal. Material searchable queries keep unknown values through filtering, report Pending, and discard drafts and menus after host replacement. Audit other choice widgets and invalid shapes.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The renderer MUST NOT select the first valid option
requirements.statement: An out-of-domain value must not be visually or structurally replaced by the first valid choice.
requirements.next: Material/Cupertino plain-enum and const-oneOf dropdowns display imported out-of-domain numbers and explicit null without selecting or writing a substitute; standard and searchable presentations expose null with an English/Bulgarian warning. Plain-enum/const-oneOf radios leave every valid option unselected and expose unknown JSON. Numeric values equivalent under JSON Schema, including nested numeric values in object and array choices, are selected without a mount write in dropdowns and radios; oneOf checkbox arrays recognize and remove the imported occurrence. Sixteen mounted numeric and structural choice cases pass on JVM, iOS, JS browser and Wasm browser. Multi-select/chips present imported non-array null as an actual current value with no selected choice and repair only after explicit selection. Add selected-state coverage for other list presentations, full browser suites and unknown shapes.

requirements.statement: Invalid existing data stays visible and editable without truncation, padding, normalization or a mount write.
requirements.next: Mounted Material/Cupertino Boolean, text, numeric, password/OTP, date/time/date-time, mixed string-or-enum, slider, color, duration, cron, null and file-control JVM cases show imported invalid JSON under English/Bulgarian markers, with no write until explicit correction. Invalid slider values are marked in accessible error semantics while the thumb remains provisional. Color picker-only and file picker/cell presentations also expose the value. Cases distinguish missing from null. Audit remaining controls, cells and non-JVM interaction.

requirements.statement: The six-field cron format is validated through normal schema validation; the control does not republish schema failures as additional errors.
requirements.next: The six-field format validator is registered with normal schema validation, including hidden controls. Four core tests pass on JVM/iOS/JS Node/Wasm browser, including unbounded positive steps and weekday 7 normalization before stepping. The imported Unix five-field and Quartz seven-field values show local feedback and recover after correction in both renderer families on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm. The renderer does not publish additional errors. Audit further selector forms and host error policy before closing.

requirements.sourceAnchor: The picker asks for a period first
requirements.statement: Cron picker periods expose only relevant fields, preserve the authored spelling when untouched, and pin only lower wildcard time fields after a valid upper-time selection.
requirements.next: Material/Cupertino picker periods and numeric field editing are mounted on JVM/iOS/JS browser/Wasm browser; pure tests cover period lenses and valid/invalid time defaults. The imported fixture now tests unchanged MON-FRI and L selectors and edits to a weekday list and numeric month day in both families across those targets. The active period exposes selected semantics and an English/Bulgarian state description in all 16 focused control cases. Verify other complex selectors, narrow geometry, keyboard focus, direct screen-reader output, real webcomponent integration and device interaction.

requirements.statement: Cron raw text stays editable and visible when invalid; staged Apply/Cancel and immediate mode obey permissions, Clear removes the value, and host replacement drops a stale picker draft.
requirements.next: Material/Cupertino mounted cases pass on JVM/iOS/JS browser/Wasm browser for invalid direct text, untouched aliases, Apply/Cancel, immediate edits, Clear, readonly, live Bulgarian locale, host replacement, disable-rule changes and invalid staged picker feedback. Ten imported fixture cases add authored schema/UI selection, unset picker cancellation, five-/seven-field repair, and unchanged/edited weekday and month-end selectors on the same targets. Verify focus/IME, real webcomponent/device input and accessible dialog semantics.

requirements.statement: Color edits serialize to hex, hex3, rgb or hsb; alpha uses hex8, rgba or hsba, and transparent hex3 edits are refused.
requirements.next: Codec and 22 mounted color cases pass JVM/iOS/JS browser/Wasm browser after Cupertino picker adopted native controls; Android main compiles. Verify Android device, actual webcomponent and physical keyboard/screen-reader behavior.

requirements.statement: Color parsing accepts short/full/alpha hex and comma-separated RGB, HSL and HSB forms, while unsupported input produces no fallback color or mount-time mutation.
requirements.next: Shared schema format validation passes JVM/iOS/JS browser/Wasm browser; mounted invalid-import, incomplete direct-text draft and HSL-to-hex normalization pass those targets. Android main compiles. Verify remaining notations through mounted text entry and Android device behavior.

requirements.statement: Disabling colorTextEntry leaves a clearable picker; the initial channel view follows the save format, and switching view alone preserves storage and data.
requirements.next: Picker-only Clear, initial Hex/RGB/HSB view, non-mutating switching/reopen reset, host replacement and readonly invalidation pass JVM/iOS/JS browser/Wasm browser with native Cupertino buttons, sliders and inputs. Android main compiles; verify device focus and visual selection.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Text entry accepts the documented notations
requirements.statement: Color text entry keeps incomplete input as a local draft, valid edits normalize to the configured save format, and schema format errors use ordinary JSON Schema validation.
requirements.next: Schema constraint, invalid-import state, local pending draft and HSL normalization pass on JVM/iOS/JS browser/Wasm browser. Verify all documented direct-text notations, focus/IME and Android behavior.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Recheck mutation permissions and target identity
requirements.statement: Delayed commits recheck current enabled, readonly, restriction and target identity before writing.
requirements.next: The extended Button rejects pending edits before its asynchronous dispatch and reads controller state at execution; numeric and dialog tests cover selected cancellation paths. Delayed edit commits across all renderer families and restriction changes need a mutation-path audit.

requirements.sourceAnchor: selection that only displays MUST NOT
requirements.statement: Display-only selection must not invoke destructive confirmation; selection that writes must use the shared confirmation policy.
requirements.next: Audit all display-only navigation and writing selections in both families, including nested list/table and branch controls; add explicit mounted no-prompt and prompt tests across targets.

requirements.statement: Picker internal and displayed values must not silently change the configured stored serialization.
requirements.next: Map all temporal and color picker save-format paths, including direct input, incomplete drafts and locale changes, to exact stored-value tests across targets.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Runtime interaction state MUST NOT mutate
requirements.statement: Category, step, expansion, splitter, action, focus, hover and widget state must remain outside the authored UI schema.
requirements.next: Add mounted identity tests for each runtime-state family, asserting UI-schema equality through interaction and rerender on all applicable targets.

requirements.sourceAnchor: editor-local state MUST NOT become form data
requirements.statement: Template-local and editor-local state must not become committed form data.
requirements.next: Test named Template/Slot local state and every pending editor draft through cancel, rerender and external replacement; verify emitted data does not gain runtime keys.

requirements.statement: Renderer-specific option namespaces must not redefine reserved portable names incompatibly.
requirements.next: Material input chrome now uses options.material.inputVariant and config.jsonformsExtended.material.inputVariant; portable variant and old top-level config.variant cannot select its style. Verify all renderer-specific consumers, other native namespaces and mounted behavior before closing.

requirements.statement: Ship an example catalogue with the portable model.
requirements.next: Finish three explicit example gaps/exclusions and validate catalogue navigation on every host.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Examples MUST use understandable business domains
requirements.statement: Examples use realistic business domains, names, labels, descriptions, data and constraints.
requirements.next: Audit each imported and native example for realistic content and record any deliberate source-preserving exceptions.

requirements.statement: Portable adapters share machine-readable conformance vectors.
requirements.next: Verify every pinned authoring and behavior vector executes through the Kotlin adapter across applicable targets; catalogue import alone is insufficient.

requirements.statement: Conformance covers prototype protection, URL policy, script gating and Markdown sanitization.
requirements.next: Map each security vector to executing Kotlin tests on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm and add missing mounted URL/Markdown/script checks.

requirements.statement: Renderer families publish missing table, pagination and detail capabilities until implemented; schema acceptance alone does not claim support.
requirements.next: Reconcile all declared table and detail variants against actual renderer registry dispatch and expose accessible diagnostics for every unsupported profile.

requirements.sourceAnchor: AG Grid controls MUST support portable
requirements.statement: An AG Grid adapter consumes portable pagination, columnDefs and rowDetail options, with explicit native settings overriding corresponding portable settings.
requirements.next: Both development and production Web Component bundles show the portable table fallback and variant.unsupported diagnostic in Chrome without a data write. Defer AG Grid conformance until a JS-only DOM adapter passes host lifecycle and browser interaction gates; this fallback does not implement AG Grid.

requirements.statement: AG Grid native page-size and column overrides apply independently and retain portable row-detail behavior.
requirements.next: Add precedence tests to a future JS-only AG Grid adapter, including explicit empty columns, false pagination and unchanged row detail.

requirements.sourceAnchor: choosing a display name MUST NOT
requirements.statement: Friendly tooling identifiers preserve their established option encodings and do not silently rewrite data schema or canonical variant.
requirements.next: The demo exposes raw JSON panes with no friendly presentation-name mapping; graphical authoring is outside the plan's initial runtime scope. Canonical UI options round-trip without changing schema or data. Reopen this row if a friendly selector is added.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Date, Time, and Date-time controls SHOULD provide
requirements.statement: Date, time and date-time controls provide discoverable preferred picker interactions that apply supported schema bounds.
requirements.next: Verify schema-bound choice disabling and picker geometry/accessibility on all targets, including Android device interaction.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Controls SHOULD also allow direct keyboard entry
requirements.statement: Temporal controls permit format-aware direct entry, show the expected format and honor mask:false where supported.
requirements.next: Eight temporal format-hint cases pass on JVM/iOS/JS/Wasm. The shared temporal option reader requires real JSON booleans. The retained 15-case date/time/Material date-time mask matrix passes on JVM; its cases passed in the earlier iOS/Wasm runs, and JS date, time and Material date-time cases pass in focused groups. Three target-specific Cupertino date-time cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator and Wasm browser. A single Cupertino date-time text replacement stalls the JS browser runner; its direct-input interaction remains unverified there. The combined JS matrix also failed to compile under low disk space. Incremental IME, locale changes, screen-reader output and Android interaction remain open.

requirements.statement: Scroll panes retain themed pointer, wheel, touch and keyboard behavior; show scrollbars only on overflow and keep both required axes reachable.
requirements.next: Audit every dialog, table, sidebar and split pane for overflow geometry, horizontal reachability and standard input on all applicable targets.

requirements.statement: Cron accepts the documented six-field grammar and selector profile, validates via normal schema validation, and does not republish those errors as additional errors.
requirements.next: Run a grammar matrix covering named months/weekdays and L/W/# selectors across targets; verify schema-owned error and no additional-error publication.

requirements.statement: Routine data and validation updates preserve the mounted editor, keyboard focus, caret/selection, IME composition and open picker for the same logical field.
requirements.next: Audit every control and cell for host echo and validation rerender identity, including IME and picker interaction on devices.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Keep row identity and cell-renderer component identity stable
requirements.statement: Table row and cell component identity follows the logical item across edits and reorders.
requirements.next: Add mounted focus and caret assertions through row update, reorder, sort and pagination on all targets.

requirements.sourceAnchor: This feedback also applies to checkbox and switch cells
requirements.statement: Boolean table cells expose their localized field error locally and clear it after a valid correction.
requirements.next: Verify mounted Boolean error semantics, correction clearing and direct screen-reader output across targets.

requirements.statement: An array child-error summary is renderer aggregation and does not replace each cell error or become an additional validator error.
requirements.next: Verify summary and cell error coexist, including off-page errors and host additional errors.

requirements.statement: ListWithDetail has a resizable vertical divider whose keyboard and focus behavior works when form data is read-only.

requirements.next: Paired Material/Cupertino mounted JVM tests show an off-page additional-property name is rejected as duplicate with no data write; off-page host and JSON Schema errors appear in page summaries and navigate to their page. Continue with sorting/filtering before paging across applicable families and targets.

requirements.statement: Paging, sorting and external replacement preserve logical edit targets, selection, focus and pending drafts.
requirements.next: Paired JVM Material/Cupertino pagination cases show host replacement cancels an additional-property rename draft, restores page navigation and clears a paged list-with-detail selection rather than redirecting it. Moving a selected list item across a page boundary, then editing its detail, updates its new index; confirming deletion of an earlier paged item shifts the selected detail to its new index. Add sort/filter identity and non-JVM pending-draft tests.

requirements.statement: Collection pager has localized keyboard-accessible controls in a distinct footer; optional top pager shares state.
requirements.next: Shared Material/Cupertino pagers use English/Bulgarian built-in navigation and error-page labels, including singular error count. Live regional Bulgarian tests pass on JVM table and list-with-detail with no writes; mounted Enter-key tests navigate forward/back in Material/Cupertino-host table pagers and the Cupertino list pager. Check narrow/RTL placement, keyboard behavior on browser/native targets and optional top-pager synchronization.

requirements.sourceAnchor: Dialog presentation adds a localized Edit details
requirements.statement: Row dialog edits an isolated whole-item draft; Apply rechecks identity and guards, Cancel discards, and read-only inspection remains available.
requirements.next: Shared English/Bulgarian defaults now cover row-dialog actions and geometry labels while preserving host translation keys. Paired mounted JVM cases verify live regional Bulgarian action/title labels with no write. Verify stale replacement, pending nested edits and translated dialog actions on other targets.

requirements.statement: Right and bottom row-detail panels default to resizable dividers and preserve selection, data, drafts, validation and size through edits.
requirements.next: Verify pending drafts, keyboard/accessibility and read-only divider behavior on devices.

requirements.statement: Collapsed is initial panel visibility; show/hide retains row selection and data and does not reset on ordinary data updates.
requirements.next: Paired Material/Cupertino mounted JVM cases verify live regional Bulgarian panel labels and show/hide without a write. Test runtime visibility persistence through edits, both placements, dialog-only option inapplicability and other-target behavior.

requirements.statement: Visible detail selection has styled and accessible current-row indication independent of bulk-delete checkbox selection.
requirements.next: The shared Material table-row renderer exposes selected=false for selectable noncurrent rows, selected=true and a localized current-row state description for the visible detail row. Paired Material/Cupertino mounted panel cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser through select, hide, reveal and page changes without a data write. Verify bulk-delete checkbox independence, direct screen-reader output, Android interaction and native Cupertino presentation.

requirements.statement: Keep serialized spec and examples independent of component libraries, share core logic, and isolate component rendering and props in adapters.
requirements.next: Audit dependencies and adapter boundaries.

requirements.statement: Verify readonly and separateReadonlyFromDisabled presentation in each adapter before claiming renderer support.
requirements.next: Paired Material/Cupertino mounted tests verify separateReadonlyFromDisabled keeps a read-only text input enabled and focusable, without a Clear action or form write. New paired cases document that read-only Boolean widgets remain disabled even when the config is true; they cannot use a text-style read-only state. The focused JVM class passes and iOS simulator test sources compile. Audit other control and cell families plus native/browser behavior before claiming general adapter support.

requirements.statement: Validate the draft-07 authoring schemas offline by their published IDs.

requirements.next: The extended UI profile validates imported nested UI schemas and registered detail UI schemas; two declared invalid fixtures reject at exact pointers before repaired copies pass. Add deeper negative layout/detail probes.

requirements.next: The common config profile accepts explicit restrict false in an offline probe. Add coverage for namespaced defaults and invalid known values.

requirements.statement: Validate extended configuration and security blocks with the extended config artifact.
requirements.next: The extended config profile validates imported configs and a security URL-policy Boolean, and rejects its quoted Boolean form. Add broader security/config negative fixtures.

requirements.next: A standalone SHOW rule validates and an invalid effect rejects under the published rule artifact. Add recursive AND/OR and both UI-profile references.

requirements.statement: Allow unknown options and namespaces while enforcing known field constraints; accept unknown extended element types for downstream registries.
requirements.next: Common and extended UI profiles preserve an unknown vendor option, reject a malformed known focus option, and the extended profile accepts an unknown downstream element type. Test additional known fields and runtime diagnostics.

requirements.statement: Do not apply authoring-schema defaults to authored UI schemas or config during validation.
requirements.next: The offline checker compares imported documents and registry entries before and after validation, and probes omitted default-bearing UI/config fields. Kotlin parser and demo Config-editor tests keep authored options/config keys absent while runtime layout defaults resolve. Extend this to additional default-bearing fields and target UI.

requirements.statement: Keep structural authoring validation distinct from semantic and runtime conformance, and never derive script permission from schema acceptance.
requirements.next: The offline authoring profile accepts script-only Buttons and structurally valid unresolved Control scopes. Mounted Material/Cupertino tests keep script execution denied until permission and report unresolved property scopes with a localized, visible non-editable fallback and no write; live schema replacement and escaped property pointers retain correct dispatch. Tuple-position scopes keep their dedicated diagnostic path. Extend this separation to other executable descriptors and cross-target UI.

requirements.statement: Check example data schemas against the applicable meta-schema, leaving custom keywords to the selected validator integration.
requirements.next: The offline gate counts 11 declared draft-07 and 34 implicit draft-07 imported data schemas, rejects a different declared dialect before validation, and probes malformed schema-type rejection by Ajv's bundled meta-schema. Audit selected runtime custom keywords and add a corresponding meta-schema path if another dialect enters the catalog.

requirements.statement: Validate each example data schema, UI schema, config, registry UI schema and metadata; enforce exact expected-invalid pointers.
requirements.next: The offline gate checks 194 imported documents or registered UI schemas, portable registry match metadata, 49 source catalog entries, only English/Bulgarian catalogs with matching keys, and exact pointers for two expected-invalid fixtures before repairs. Add Kotlin host semantics and deeper negative cases.

requirements.statement: Use the same data/schema semantics, registries, config, locale, validation mode and action contracts in native and web-component hosts.
requirements.next: Chrome passes all 14 demo URL scenarios and the standalone Web Component scenario, including edited-data host round trips, settings, server-error actions, mounted action completion, authored additional-errors, validation-mode changes and rendered light/dark/system themes. A nested edit from absent data emits dataProvided=true after a portable reducer fix; core JVM tests and Wasm/iOS main compilation pass. A direct JavaScript uiSchemaRegistry property accepts tester functions with schema, schemaPath and path arguments; Chrome verifies nested object detail selection, same-array tester replacement and fallback after clearing. A real pre-upgrade property assignment retains its function and later setter refresh; a throwing tester falls back and emits a path-bearing diagnostic. Development and production bundles pass; all 12 Node registration tests pass. The iframe JSON attribute bridge still cannot carry tester functions and displays a notice; named UI schemas continue to transfer there. Only English and Bulgarian ship. Offline Android resolution lacks AndroidX artifacts. Compare renderer/cell registry customization, remaining settings, accessibility and target behavior with native hosts before claiming full parity.

requirements.statement: Preserve current data and settings when switching hosts.
requirements.next: The extracted bridge uses current Compose form state and settings rather than original example data; six JVM tests cover edited and missing data, validation mode, config overrides, readonly, direction, locale/form-locale override, dark theme, catalogs, host errors and warning state. The JS overlay returns data and dataProvided changes to the same parent state. Chrome tests pass Web-Component-to-Compose-and-back round trips for edited data, the Job form's Bulgarian locale and toggled theme, RTL direction and Validate And Hide. A mounted Chrome run also preserves absent data across a host switch, accepts a real nested Web Component text edit, and preserves the resulting provided data after another switch. The application chrome stays English during the Job action. Add mounted round trips for remaining settings before claiming complete preservation across hosts.

requirements.statement: Install component styles in the ShadowRoot and support styled portals, workers and overlays.
requirements.next: The Web Component opens a ShadowRoot and gives its child host to ComposeViewport's HTMLElement overload; Compose installs canvas and backing-input styles in its own nested shadow tree. Chrome asserts an empty light DOM, a visible canvas and backing-input style. A plain text field remains accessible after detaching and reinserting the same element. A regression found that reconnect had overwritten a local edit with an unchanged host data attribute; the refresh path now retains local data until the host writes data or data-provided, including while detached. Chrome verifies one viewport, one change from the retained value, and a detached same-value host reset before the next edit. Both development and production bundles pass this standalone Chrome test; all 14 demo URL scenarios pass with the development bundle. A later Material enum popup remains under the component shadow ancestry and writes data when clicked. After enum selection, Chrome's accessibility tree still shows the popup layer and no textbox; Escape and an outside click do not restore it during focused probes. Forcing the renderer's menu subtree to unmount had the same result and was reverted. Investigate Compose Web popup/accessibility synchronization, worker loading and other portal types before marking complete. The public ComposeViewport overload exposes no disposal handle for a true unmount.

requirements.statement: Follow selected light, dark and system color scheme, including system changes after mount.
requirements.next: The Web Component resolves explicit light/dark and system media preference and refreshes on changes. The mounted Chrome test passes visual button-region comparisons for explicit and emulated system preference changes after mount; 10 Node registration tests and Kotlin JS compilation also pass. Verify native/demo color-scheme hosts before claiming all-host support.

requirements.statement: Use real library controls where available and preserve keyboard, focus and theme contracts when adapting primitives.
requirements.next: Audit each adapted control through interaction tests.

requirements.statement: Expose example, live data, schema, UI schema, registered UI schemas, translations and config in the demo.
requirements.next: Mounted JVM workflows reach Data, Schema, UI Schema, UI Schemas, Internationalization and Config editor views and observe their effects in the Demo form. Check example selection, pane geometry, accessibility and other-target runtime.

requirements.statement: Give JSON editors Reload and Apply; invalid JSON leaves active state intact; Apply changes only the edited property; Reload does not apply.
requirements.next: Paired Material/Cupertino-style mounted JVM tests cover invalid Apply, valid Apply and nonapplying Reload for all six JSON editor panes. Data drafts track unapplied changes: tabbed and simultaneous Demo/Data form edits retain dirty or reloaded-original drafts, while clean drafts refresh after compact JSON Apply. Every pane exposes an accessible error after invalid Apply, clears it on Reload and leaves the form intact; Data also clears it on edit. Keyboard tests reach Reload, Apply and the Data editor input with Tab. Bulgarian Data Apply failure now has a localized explanation in visible and accessible feedback while retaining parser detail; English behavior remains. The focused JVM suite passes and iOS simulator test sources compile. Verify other-target runtime, focus across the remaining panes and direct screen-reader behavior.

requirements.statement: Start form/data panes near 75/25 with resizable, keyboard-usable minima, RTL direction and narrow stacking.
requirements.next: JVM mounted split-pane tests verify initial wide 75/25 geometry, minimum widths, narrow stacking, progress/keyboard/touch resizing and RTL direction; paired full-workspace tests edit form and Data JSON simultaneously. Check browser/native pointer and keyboard focus and screen-reader semantics.

requirements.statement: Preserve data and settings through form-only mode and back.
requirements.next: Paired Material/Cupertino-style mounted JVM tests edit the form, enter form-only mode, return to the full workspace, and retain both data and Bulgarian locale selection. Existing URL-host test preserves data and readonly state through external mode changes. Verify browser back/forward, native host lifecycle and settings changed during form-only transitions.

requirements.statement: Expose theme, direction, locale, readonly, validation, default restricted edits, description and required-marker settings separately from library settings.
requirements.next: The Settings overlay exposes theme, direction, English/Bulgarian locale, validation, layout and common behavior controls. Paired Material/Cupertino-style mounted JVM tests verify Read-Only changes field editability without changing data; pure tests cover preference defaults and config overlays, and paired form tests cover error-filter and additional-property overrides. Verify browser/native settings interactions and all controls end to end.

requirements.statement: Provide stable example links and feature groups; show error count with schema, additional and pending analysis distinguishable.
requirements.next: All built-in examples have curated feature groups and retain their stable IDs; paired mounted JVM tests navigate groups in English and Bulgarian. The summary distinguishes schema and host additional errors and now shows live renderer-owned pending analysis separately from the confirmed error count. Paired date-draft tests verify pending clears on correction, pane unmount and example change, then returns for a new draft. Verify browser/native navigation, screen-reader semantics and deep-link handling with group filters before marking supported.

requirements.statement: Make every interactive element keyboard reachable with a visible focus indicator.
requirements.next: Grouped demo entries expose selected semantics, a 3 dp focus border and keyboard Enter activation in paired Material/Cupertino-style JVM tests; Tab moves from sidebar search to the first example. Settings focus cycling and splitter keyboard resize have separate tests. A Chrome Settings-panel probe showed the Compose accessibility DOM containing only the active popup (close tooltip or Direction menu), not the visible underlying Settings controls. A pointer-only panel experiment did not change this and was reverted. Audit browser keyboard traversal and screen-reader output, plus every renderer/cell role and native targets, before marking supported.

requirements.statement: Give icon actions localized names and focusable tooltips; manage and restore dialog focus.
requirements.next: The shared demo toolbar tooltip now opens on focus and dismisses when focus moves; paired mounted JVM tests verify English/Bulgarian icon names and tooltip text. Paired Material/Cupertino row-detail tests verify focus enters the dialog frame and returns to the Edit details trigger on cancel; settings overlay focus restoration also passes. Audit remaining icon actions/dialogs and browser/native focus behavior before marking supported.

requirements.statement: Expose disclosure, selection, disabled, required and error state through platform semantics without relying on color.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM tests cover Group expanded/collapsed state, localized error semantics on a collapsed Group disclosure that clear after correction, selected demo example state, and required/error semantics on representative controls. Disabled action semantics have focused coverage elsewhere. Material and Cupertino text inputs now attach visible labels to editable semantics; paired mounted JVM tests pass, and the rebuilt Web Component Chrome scenario locates Legal name by its accessible name after an absent-data host switch. All 14 demo Chrome URL scenarios pass. Audit remaining renderer and cell roles, especially disabled/read-only and composite selection states, plus native accessibility before marking supported.

requirements.statement: Cover controls, overlays, editors, validation and icons in both themes; use logical inline RTL without changing data paths.
requirements.next: Paired mounted JVM tests change Light/Dark theme and LTR/RTL direction through Settings, verify selected semantics, move the sidebar to the logical RTL side and retain form data. Provider tests confirm Material/Cupertino background and surface palettes change with dark mode and propagate RTL. Split-pane RTL resize has separate coverage. Inspect actual control, overlay, editor, validation and icon rendering in both themes on browser/native targets before marking supported.

requirements.statement: Test competing dispatch through the full registry for values, restrictions, readonly, hidden, empty/absent, locale, drafts, external updates and identity.
requirements.next: Pure full-registry ranking tests cover conflicting schema/UI formats. Paired mounted JVM tests verify UI color beats schema password through the complete Material/Cupertino extended registries, including pending draft retention, readonly, Bulgarian labels, typed JSON commit, sibling identity and host replacement. New paired tests keep this conflicting control hidden until its rule matches, open it with an absent value, commit one color, hide it again and reflect a later host replacement without extra writes; focused JVM tests pass and iOS simulator test sources compile. The targeted iOS simulator run stopped during linking with disk-full errno 28 before tests executed. Existing full-registry color/null/code tests cover additional cases. Expand to other conflicting renderers and cells, then run browser/native integration before marking supported.

requirements.statement: Verify scalar controls and table cells through their respective registries and assert JSON shapes and emitted values.
requirements.next: Paired mounted Material/Cupertino table tests verify plain integer, number, explicit enum, scalar string/number const, const-only oneOf, authored radio, opt-in slider and date/time/date-time cell selection, wrong-type import retention, bounded numeric drafts, host replacement, duplicate choice titles and typed emissions on JVM, iOS and focused browsers. Host-controlled read-only transitions pass for selector and radio cells; radio cells prefer enum options when both enum and oneOf occur. Boolean const agreements keep their toggle path. Compact cron, duration and color cells select through both extended cell registries. JVM mounted tests cover row-specific writes, picker cancellation, Bulgarian action labels and readonly; color also covers invalid draft retention, host replacement, picker-only swatch commits and clearing a stale draft after host row reordering. Compact cron/duration cells now keep their picker trigger with showActions:false, commit component edits immediately, retain the open editor after the commit, and dismiss it on readonly in both families. Six further mounted cases verify each UI cell format beats a conflicting schema password format in both families, preserves a sibling on edit, remains inert on absent host replacement and exposes wrong-type import feedback. Common tests compile for iOS. Expand to hidden, other identity transitions, other registry conflicts and browser/native runtime; clean full-browser reporting remains open.

requirements.statement: Build packages, demos and web components separately and test theme, RTL, narrow and ShadowRoot behavior where applicable.
requirements.next: The test-task manifest separates JVM, iOS simulator, JS/Wasm browser, Android device, Xcode host-link, production bundle and webcomponent host gates. The full 2,080-case demo JVM suite passes; focused theme/RTL and split-pane JVM cases and one production-bundle webcomponent browser case have recorded evidence. Separate final package/demo/webcomponent builds, narrow browser and ShadowRoot overlays, device interaction, native host link and full browser suites remain open.
